title.zh: 卷九十六 列傳第四十六: 姚崇 宋璟
title.en: Volume 96 Biographies 46: Yao Chong, Song Jing
title.raw: 卷九十六 列傳第四十六: 姚崇 宋璟 Volume 96 Biographies 46: Yao Chong, Song Jing

sentences.zh: 尹思貞尹思貞，京兆長安人也。

translations.literal: Yin Sizhen—Yin Sizhen was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Sizhen was a native of Chang'an in the Jingzhao region.

sentences.zh: 弱冠明經舉，補隆州參軍。

translations.literal: At the age of twenty he passed the Mingjing examination and was appointed aide in Long Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In his early twenties he passed the Classics examination and was appointed military aide in Long Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時晉安縣有豪族蒲氏，縱橫不法，前後官吏莫能制。

translations.literal: At that time in Jin'an County there was a powerful clan, the Pu, who acted lawlessly in every direction, and none of the officials before or after could restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the powerful Pu clan in Jin'an County ran roughshod over the law, and no official before or after him had been able to bring them to heel.

sentences.zh: 州司令思貞推按，發其奸贓萬計，竟論殺之，遠近稱慶，刻石以紀其事，由是知名。

translations.literal: The prefectural administration ordered Sizhen to investigate; he uncovered their crimes and embezzlements numbering in the tens of thousands, and in the end had them sentenced to death. Near and far rejoiced, and a stone was carved to record the affair; from this he became renowned.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture ordered Sizhen to investigate; he exposed their crimes and embezzlements on a vast scale and ultimately secured their execution. People near and far celebrated, and a stone monument was erected to commemorate the case, after which he became widely known.

sentences.zh: 累轉明堂令，以善政聞。

translations.literal: He was transferred in succession to be Director of the Bright Hall and became known for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to Director of the Bright Hall and earned a reputation for sound administration.

sentences.zh: 三遷殿中少監，檢校洺州刺史。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became Vice Director of the Palace Domestic Service and acting Governor of Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he became Vice Director of the Palace Domestic Service and acting governor of Ming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會契丹孫萬榮作亂，河朔不安，思貞善於綏撫，境內獨無驚擾，則天降璽書褒美之。

translations.literal: When the Khitan Sun Wanrong rose in rebellion and the Hebei region was unsettled, Sizhen was skilled at pacification; within his jurisdiction alone there was no alarm or disturbance, and the court sent down an imperial edict with a seal to praise him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan leader Sun Wanrong rebelled and threw the Hebei region into turmoil, Sizhen excelled at pacifying the people; his jurisdiction alone remained undisturbed, and the court sent down an imperial commendation bearing the imperial seal.

sentences.zh: 長安中，七遷秋官侍郎，以忤張昌宗被構，出爲定州刺史，轉晉州刺史。

translations.literal: During the Chang'an era he was promoted seven times to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Justice; because he offended Zhang Changzong he was framed and sent out as Governor of Ding Prefecture, then transferred to Governor of Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an reign he was promoted seven times to Vice Minister of Justice; after offending Zhang Changzong he was framed and demoted to governor of Ding Prefecture, then transferred to governor of Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 尋復入爲司府少卿。

translations.literal: Before long he returned to the capital as Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled to the capital as Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 時卿侯知一亦厲威嚴，吏人爲之語曰：「不畏侯卿杖，惟畏尹卿筆。」

translations.literal: At that time the Vice Minister Hou Zhiyi was also severe in authority, and the clerks and staff had a saying: 'We do not fear Vice Minister Hou's staff—we only fear Vice Minister Yin's brush.'
translations.idiomatic: At that time Vice Minister Hou Zhiyi was also feared for his severity, and the clerks had a saying: 'We do not fear Vice Minister Hou's rod—we only fear Vice Minister Yin's pen.'

sentences.zh: 其爲人所伏若此。

translations.literal: Such was the degree to which people submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the degree to which people submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 尋加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Before long he was given the additional title of Grand Master with Silver-Green Tally.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was granted the additional title of Grand Master with Silver-Green Tally.

sentences.zh: 於宅中掘得古戟十二，俄而門加棨戟，時人異焉。

translations.literal: In his residence twelve ancient halberds were dug up; soon afterward halberds were added at his gate, and people of the time regarded it as strange.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve ancient halberds were unearthed at his residence; soon afterward ceremonial halberds were placed at his gate, and contemporaries took it as an omen.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，爲大理卿，時武三思擅權，御史大夫李承嘉附會之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shenlong era he became Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review; at that time Wu Sansi monopolized power, and the Censor-in-Chief Li Chengjia curried favor with him.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shenlong era he became Chief Minister of the Court of Judicial Review; Wu Sansi then held unchecked power, and Censor-in-Chief Li Chengjia sided with him.

sentences.zh: 壅州人韋月將上變，告三思謀逆，中宗大怒，命斬之。

translations.literal: Wei Yuejiang of Yong Prefecture submitted a memorial reporting a plot, accusing Sansi of treason; Emperor Zhongzong was greatly angered and ordered him beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yuejiang of Yong Prefecture submitted a memorial accusing Sansi of treason; Emperor Zhongzong was furious and ordered his execution.

sentences.zh: 思貞以發生之月，固執奏以爲不可行刑，竟有敕決杖配流嶺南。

translations.literal: Sizhen, on the ground that it was the month of new growth, firmly memorialized that execution could not be carried out; in the end an edict ordered him beaten with the rod and banished to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhen argued that, because it was the season of spring growth, execution was impermissible and firmly memorialized to that effect; in the end an edict ordered Wei beaten and exiled to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 三思令所司因此非法害之，思貞又固爭之。

translations.literal: Sansi ordered the responsible offices to harm him unlawfully on this pretext, and Sizhen again firmly contested it.
translations.idiomatic: Sansi then ordered the responsible offices to harm Wei by unlawful means on this pretext, and Sizhen again contested the matter firmly.

sentences.zh: 承嘉希三思旨，托以他事，不許思貞入朝廷。

translations.literal: Chengjia, hoping to please Sansi's intent, used another matter as a pretext and did not allow Sizhen to enter the court.
translations.idiomatic: Chengjia, eager to please Sansi, used another matter as a pretext to bar Sizhen from attending court.

sentences.zh: 謂承嘉曰：「公擅作威福，不顧憲章，附托奸臣，以圖不軌，將先除忠良以自恣耶？」

translations.literal: He said to Chengjia: 'You arrogate authority and favor, heedless of the statutes; you attach yourself to treacherous ministers and plot sedition—do you intend first to remove the loyal and good so that you may indulge yourself?'
translations.idiomatic: He said to Chengjia: 'You arrogate power and favor with no regard for the law; you rely on treacherous ministers and plot sedition—do you mean first to eliminate the loyal so that you may do as you please?'

sentences.zh: 承嘉大怒，遂劾奏思貞，出爲青州刺史。

translations.literal: Chengjia was greatly angered and thereupon impeached and memorialized against Sizhen, who was sent out as Governor of Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chengjia was furious and impeached Sizhen, who was demoted to governor of Qing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 境內有蠶一年四熟者，黜陟使、衞州司馬路敬潛八月至州，見繭嘆曰：「非善政所致，孰能至於此乎！」

translations.literal: Within the jurisdiction there were silkworms that matured four times in a year; the promotion-and-demotion commissioner and Wei Prefecture Senior Administrator Lu Jingqian arrived at the prefecture in the eighth month, saw the cocoons, and sighed: 'If this were not brought about by good government, who could reach such a thing!'
translations.idiomatic: Within his jurisdiction silkworms yielded four harvests in a year; Lu Jingqian, the promotion-and-demotion commissioner and senior administrator of Wei Prefecture, arrived in the eighth month, saw the cocoons, and exclaimed: 'Only good government could produce such a result!'

sentences.zh: 特表薦之。

translations.literal: He submitted a special memorial recommending him.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a special memorial recommending Sizhen.

sentences.zh: 思貞前後爲十三州刺史，皆以清簡爲政，奏課連最。

translations.literal: Sizhen successively served as governor of thirteen prefectures, in all cases governing with purity and simplicity, and his submitted evaluations were continuously ranked highest.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhen served successively as governor of thirteen prefectures, governing each with austerity and integrity, and his performance reports consistently ranked first.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，徵爲將作大匠，累封天水郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, Sizhen was summoned as Director of Palace Buildings and was enfeoffed in succession as Duke of Tianshui Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong acceded to the throne, Sizhen was summoned as Director of Palace Buildings and was enfeoffed as Duke of Tianshui Commandery.

sentences.zh: 時左僕射竇懷貞興造金仙、玉真兩觀，調發夫匠，思貞常節減之。

translations.literal: At that time the Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Dou Huaizhen undertook construction of the Golden Immortal and Jade Perfected monasteries and requisitioned laborers and artisans; Sizhen often reduced the numbers.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Left Vice Director Dou Huaizhen undertook construction of the Golden Immortal and Jade Perfected monasteries and requisitioned laborers; Sizhen regularly cut back the numbers assigned.

sentences.zh: 懷貞怒，頻詰責思貞，思貞曰：「公職居端揆，任重弼諧，不能翼贊聖明，光宣大化，而乃盛興土木，害及黎元，豈不愧也！

translations.literal: Huaizhen was angry and repeatedly interrogated and reproached Sizhen. Sizhen said: 'Your office stands at the head of the administration; your burden is heavy in assisting and harmonizing. You cannot wing and support the sage brilliance or broadly proclaim the great transformation, yet you lavishly raise earth and timber and harm reaches the common people—are you not ashamed!
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhen was furious and repeatedly rebuked him. Sizhen said: 'You hold the highest office in the state and bear heavy responsibility for assisting the throne; you cannot support enlightened rule or advance great reform, yet you lavishly raise grand construction projects that harm the people—are you not ashamed?

sentences.zh: 又受小人之譖，輕辱朝臣，今日之事，不能茍免，請從此辭。」

translations.literal: Moreover you accept the slanders of petty men and lightly insult court officials. In today's affair I cannot escape with my life—please accept my resignation from this point.'
translations.idiomatic: You also heed the slanders of petty men and lightly insult court officials. In today's matter I cannot let this pass—please accept my resignation here and now.'

sentences.zh: 拂衣而去，闔門累日，上聞而特令視事。

translations.literal: He brushed his robe and left; he closed his gate for several days. When the emperor heard of it, he specially ordered him to resume his duties.
translations.idiomatic: He brushed off his robes and left; he shut his gate for several days. When the emperor heard of it, he specially ordered Sizhen to resume his duties.

sentences.zh: 其年，懷貞伏誅，乃下制曰：「國之副相，位亞中臺，自匪邦直，孰司天憲？

translations.literal: That year Huaizhen was executed, and an edict was issued saying: 'The state's deputy minister stands second to the central secretariat; if he is not upright for the realm, who shall administer Heaven's laws?
translations.idiomatic: That year Huaizhen was executed, and an edict was issued: 'The state's deputy minister stands second only to the central secretariat; if he is not upright, who shall uphold the laws of the realm?

sentences.zh: 將作大匠尹思貞，賢良方正，碩儒耆德，剛不護缺，清而畏知，簡言易從，莊色難犯。

translations.literal: The Director of Palace Buildings Yin Sizhen is worthy and upright, a great scholar of venerable virtue; firm and not shielding faults, pure and yet feared for his knowledge; his brief words are easy to follow, his stern countenance hard to offend.
translations.idiomatic: Director of Palace Buildings Yin Sizhen is worthy and upright, a great scholar of venerable virtue; he is firm and does not cover faults, pure yet so respected that men fear him; his words are concise and persuasive, his bearing stern and not to be challenged.

sentences.zh: 征先王之體要，敷衽必陳；

translations.literal: When citing the essential principles of former kings, he spreads his lapels and must set them forth;
translations.idiomatic: When he expounds the essential principles of former kings, he lays them out without reserve;

sentences.zh: 折佞臣之怙權，拂衣而謝。

translations.literal: when rebuking powerful flatterers who rely on authority, he brushes his robe and takes leave.
translations.idiomatic: when he confronts powerful flatterers who abuse their authority, he brushes off his robes and resigns on the spot.

sentences.zh: 故以事聞海內，名動京師，鷹隼是擊，豺狼自遠。

translations.literal: Therefore his deeds are known within the seas, his name moves the capital; he is an eagle or falcon in striking, and wolves and jackals keep their distance of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Thus his deeds are known throughout the realm and his name resounds in the capital; like an eagle or falcon he strikes down wrongdoing, and wolves and jackals keep their distance of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 必能條理前弊，發揮舊章，宜承弄印之榮，式允登車之志。

translations.literal: He will surely be able to set in order former abuses and bring forth the old statutes; he should receive the honor of wielding the seal and fully fulfill the ambition of mounting the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: He will surely be able to rectify past abuses and restore established law; he should receive the honor of wielding the censor's seal and fulfill his long-standing ambition to serve in high office.

sentences.zh: 可御史大夫。」

translations.literal: He is approved as Censor-in-Chief.'
translations.idiomatic: He is appointed Censor-in-Chief.'

sentences.zh: 俄兼申王府長史，遷戸部尚書，轉工部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long he also served as Chief Administrator of the Prince of Shen's household, was promoted to Minister of Revenue, and transferred to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he also served as chief administrator of the Prince of Shen's household, was promoted to Minister of Revenue, and then transferred to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 以老疾累表請致仕，許之。

translations.literal: Because of age and illness he repeatedly memorialized requesting retirement, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: On account of age and illness he repeatedly memorialized requesting retirement, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 開元四年卒，年七十七，贈黃門監，謚曰簡。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaiyuan he died, aged seventy-seven; he was posthumously given the office of Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat, with the posthumous title Jian (Simple).
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Kaiyuan, aged seventy-seven; he was posthumously appointed Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat and given the posthumous title Jian (Simple).

sentences.zh: 李傑李傑，本名務光，相州滏陽人。

translations.literal: Li Jie—Li Jie, original name Wuguang, was a native of Fuyang in Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jie, whose original name was Wuguang, was a native of Fuyang in Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 後魏并州刺史寶之後也，其先自隴西徙焉。

translations.literal: He was a descendant of Bao, Governor of Bing Prefecture under Later Wei; his ancestors had moved there from Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was a descendant of Bao, governor of Bing Prefecture under the Northern Wei; his forebears had migrated there from Longxi.

sentences.zh: 傑少以孝友著稱，舉明經，累遷天官員外郎，明敏有吏才，甚得當時之譽。

translations.literal: Jie in youth was famed for filial piety and friendship; he passed the Mingjing examination and was promoted in succession to Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel; he was bright and keen and had talent for administration, and greatly won the praise of his time.
translations.idiomatic: Jie was known from youth for filial piety and brotherly devotion; he passed the Classics examination and rose to Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel. Clever and capable in administrative affairs, he won great acclaim in his day.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，累遷衞尉少卿，爲河東道巡察黜陟使，奏課爲諸使之最。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong he was promoted in succession to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud; he served as promotion-and-demotion commissioner for the Hedong circuit, and his submitted evaluation was ranked highest among all commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shenlong era he rose to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and served as promotion-and-demotion commissioner for the Hedong circuit; his performance report ranked first among all such commissioners.

sentences.zh: 開元初，爲河南尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he became Intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he was appointed Intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 傑既勤於聽理，毎有訴列，雖衢路當食，無廢處斷。

translations.literal: Jie was diligent in hearing cases; whenever there were petitions, even if he was eating in the public road he did not cease deciding them.
translations.idiomatic: Jie was diligent in hearing cases; whenever litigants appeared, he would not stop adjudicating even if he had to do so in the street while taking his meal.

sentences.zh: 由是官無留事，人吏愛之。

translations.literal: From this the offices had no backlog of business, and the people and clerks loved him.
translations.idiomatic: As a result no cases were left pending in the offices, and officials and commoners alike admired him.

sentences.zh: 先是，河、汴之間有梁公堰，年久堰破，江、淮漕運不通。

translations.literal: Earlier, between the Yellow and Bian rivers there was the Duke of Liang's weir; after many years the weir broke, and transport on the Yangtze and Huai grain routes was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, between the Yellow and Bian rivers stood the Duke of Liang's weir; after many years it collapsed, cutting off grain transport between the Yangtze-Huai region and the capital.

sentences.zh: 傑奏調發汴、鄭丁夫以浚之，省功速就，公私深以爲利，刊石水濱，以紀其績。

translations.literal: Jie memorialized to requisition laborers from Bian and Zheng to dredge it; labor was economized and the work was quickly completed; public and private interests deeply benefited, and a stone was carved on the riverbank to record his achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Jie memorialized to mobilize laborers from Bian and Zheng to dredge the channel; the work was completed quickly with minimal expenditure, to the great benefit of public and private interests alike, and a stone inscription was erected on the riverbank to commemorate his achievement.

sentences.zh: 尋代宋璟爲御史大夫。

translations.literal: Before long he replaced Song Jing as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he succeeded Song Jing as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 時皇后妹婿尚衣奉御長孫昕與其妹婿楊仙玉因於裏巷遇傑，遂毆擊之，上大怒，令斬昕等。

translations.literal: At that time the empress's sister's husband, Director of Palace Attendants Zhangsun Xin, and her other sister's husband Yang Xianyu encountered Jie in a back lane and thereupon beat him. The emperor was greatly angered and ordered Xin and the others beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhangsun Xin, Director of Palace Attendants and brother-in-law of the empress, and Yang Xianyu, another of the empress's brothers-in-law, encountered Jie in a lane and assaulted him. The emperor was furious and ordered Xin and the others executed.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍馬情素以爲陽和之月，不可行刑，累表陳請。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Ma Qingsu held that in the month of yang harmony execution could not be carried out, and repeatedly submitted memorials pleading this.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Ma Qingsu argued that in the season of spring growth executions were impermissible and repeatedly submitted memorials pleading for mercy.

sentences.zh: 乃下敕曰：「夫爲令者自近而及遠，行罰者先親而後疏。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued saying: 'One who makes laws begins with what is near and extends to what is far; one who carries out punishments begins with kin and then proceeds to those more distant.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then issued: 'He who makes laws begins with what is near and extends to what is far; he who carries out punishments begins with kin and then proceeds to those more distant.

sentences.zh: 長孫昕、楊仙玉等憑恃姻戚，恣行凶險，輕侮常憲，損辱大臣，情特難容，故令斬決。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Xin, Yang Xianyu, and the others relied on their marriage ties, wantonly committed violence and treachery, lightly insulted the regular statutes, and harmed and insulted a great minister; the circumstances were especially hard to tolerate, and therefore they were ordered beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Xin, Yang Xianyu, and the others relied on their marriage connections, committed wanton violence, showed contempt for the law, and insulted a high minister; the circumstances were especially intolerable, and therefore they were ordered executed.

sentences.zh: 今群官等累陳表疏，固有誠請，以陽和之節，非肅殺之時，援引古今，詞義懇切。

translations.literal: Now the assembled officials have repeatedly submitted memorials; they truly have sincere pleas, holding that in the season of yang harmony it is not the time of stern killing, citing ancient and modern precedents with earnest and sincere wording.
translations.idiomatic: Now the assembled officials have repeatedly submitted memorials with sincere pleas, arguing that the season of spring growth is not a time for stern executions, citing ancient and modern precedents in earnest and persuasive language.

sentences.zh: 朕志從深諫，情亦惜法，宜寬異門之罰，聽從枯木之斃。

translations.literal: Our will follows their deep remonstrance; Our feelings also cherish the law. The punishment of those outside Our clan should be widened, and We should heed the plea that withered wood not be killed.
translations.idiomatic: Our will follows their earnest remonstrance, and Our feelings also incline toward mercy under the law; the punishment of those outside Our clan should be moderated, and We should heed the plea that withered wood not be cut down in spring.

sentences.zh: 即宜決殺，以謝百僚。」

translations.literal: They should forthwith be decisively executed to answer the hundred officials.'
translations.idiomatic: They are forthwith to be executed, to satisfy the court.'

sentences.zh: 傑明年以護橋陵作，賜爵武威子。

translations.literal: The next year Jie, for supervising construction at Qiaoling, was granted the title Viscount of Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Jie was granted the title Viscount of Wuwei for supervising construction at Qiaoling.

sentences.zh: 初，傑護作時，引侍御史王旭爲判官。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jie was supervising the construction, he brought in Attending Censor Wang Xu as judge.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Jie was supervising the construction, he appointed Attending Censor Wang Xu as his aide.

sentences.zh: 旭貪冒受贓，傑將繩之而不得其實，反爲旭所構，出爲衢州刺史。

translations.literal: Xu was greedy and accepted bribes; Jie was about to punish him but could not obtain proof of the facts, and on the contrary was framed by Xu and sent out as Governor of Qu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was corrupt and accepted bribes; Jie tried to prosecute him but could not obtain proof, and was instead framed by Xu and demoted to governor of Qu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 俄轉揚州大都督府長史，又爲御史所劾，免官歸第。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Senior Administrator of the Yangzhou Metropolitan Area Command; he was again impeached by censors, dismissed from office, and returned to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to senior administrator of the Yangzhou metropolitan command, but was again impeached by censors, dismissed from office, and sent home.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，贈戸部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long he died and was posthumously given the office of Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward and was posthumously appointed Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 解琬解琬，魏州元城人也。

translations.literal: Xie Wan—Xie Wan was a native of Yuancheng in Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Wan was a native of Yuancheng in Wei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少應幽素舉，拜新政尉，累轉成都丞。

translations.literal: In youth he responded to the Yousu examination and was appointed magistrate of Xinzheng; he was transferred in succession to Assistant Magistrate of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he passed the Yousu examination and was appointed magistrate of Xinzheng; he rose in succession to assistant magistrate of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 因奏事稱旨，超遷監察御史，丁憂離職。

translations.literal: Because his memorial on state affairs pleased the emperor, he was promoted out of turn to Investigating Censor; he left office on account of mourning for a parent.
translations.idiomatic: Because a memorial on state affairs pleased the throne, he was promoted out of turn to Investigating Censor; he then left office to observe mourning for a parent.

sentences.zh: 則天以琬識練邊事，起復舊官，令往西域安撫夷虜，抗疏固辭。

translations.literal: Empress Wu, because Wan was versed and practiced in frontier affairs, recalled him to his former office and ordered him to go to the Western Regions to pacify the barbarians; he submitted a forthright memorial firmly declining.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu, recognizing Wan's expertise in frontier affairs, recalled him to his former post and ordered him to the Western Regions to pacify the barbarians; he submitted a forthright memorial firmly declining.

sentences.zh: 則天嘉之，下敕曰：「解琬孝性淳至，哀情懇切，固辭權奪之榮，乞就終憂之典。

translations.literal: Empress Wu commended this and issued an edict saying: 'Xie Wan's filial nature is pure and utmost; his grief is earnest and sincere. He firmly declines the honor of being recalled from mourning and begs to complete the full rites of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The empress commended him and issued an edict: 'Xie Wan's filial nature is pure and sincere, and his grief is earnest; he firmly declines the honor of being recalled from mourning and begs to complete the full mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 足可以激揚風俗，敦獎名教，宜遂雅懷，允其所請。

translations.literal: This is fully sufficient to rouse and uplift custom and to encourage and reward the teachings of proper names; his refined wish should be followed and his request granted.
translations.idiomatic: This is sufficient to uplift public morals and encourage proper conduct; his wish should be honored and his request granted.

sentences.zh: 仍令服闋後赴上。」

translations.literal: He was still ordered to come to court after the mourning period ended.'
translations.idiomatic: He was nevertheless ordered to report to court after his mourning period ended.'

sentences.zh: 聖歷初，遷侍御史，充使安撫烏質勒及十姓部落，咸得其便宜，蕃人大悅，以功擢拜御史中丞，兼北庭都護、持節西域安撫使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenglì he was promoted to Attending Censor and commissioned as envoy to pacify Wuzhile and the Ten Surnames tribes; all obtained suitable arrangements, and the barbarians were greatly pleased. For his merit he was promoted and appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief, concurrently Protector-General of Beiting and Commissioner with Full Powers for Pacification of the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shenglì era he was promoted to Attending Censor and commissioned to pacify Wuzhile and the Ten Surnames tribes; all parties received fair treatment, and the frontier peoples were greatly pleased. For his achievements he was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief, concurrently serving as Protector-General of Beiting and Commissioner with Full Powers for Pacification of the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 琬素與郭元振同官相善，遂爲宗楚客所毀，由是左遷滄州刺史。

translations.literal: Wan had long held the same office as Guo Yuanzhen and was on good terms with him; he was thereupon slandered by Zong Chuke and for this reason was demoted to Governor of Cang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wan had long been on friendly terms with Guo Yuanzhen, who held a similar post; he was then slandered by Zong Chuke and demoted to governor of Cang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 爲政務存大體，甚得人和。

translations.literal: In governing he strove to preserve the great essentials and greatly won human harmony.
translations.idiomatic: In administration he focused on essentials and won broad popular support.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，遷右臺御史大夫，兼持節朔方行軍大總管。

translations.literal: During Jinglong he was promoted to Censor-in-Chief of the Right Bureau and concurrently given the tally as Grand General of the Mobile Army of Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jinglong era he was promoted to Censor-in-Chief of the Right Bureau and concurrently appointed Grand General of the Mobile Army of Shuofang with full powers.

sentences.zh: 琬前後在軍二十餘載，務農習戰，多所利益，邊境安之。

translations.literal: Wan was in the army for more than twenty years before and after; he devoted himself to agriculture and trained for battle, brought many benefits, and the frontier borders were secure.
translations.idiomatic: Wan spent more than twenty years in military service altogether; he promoted agriculture and military training, brought many benefits, and kept the frontier secure.

sentences.zh: 景雲二年，復爲朔方軍大總管。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingyun he again became Grand General of the Shuofang Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingyun he again became Grand General of the Shuofang Army.

sentences.zh: 琬分遣隨軍要籍官河陽丞張冠宗、肥鄕令韋景駿、普安令於處忠等校料三城兵募，於是減十萬人，奏罷之。

translations.literal: Wan dispatched with the army the registry officer Assistant Magistrate of Heyang Zhang Guanzong, Magistrate of Feixiang Wei Jingjun, Magistrate of Pu'an Yu Chuzhong, and others to examine and verify the military levies of the three cities; thereby one hundred thousand men were reduced, and he memorialized to abolish them.
translations.idiomatic: Wan dispatched registry officer Zhang Guanzong, assistant magistrate of Heyang, Magistrate Wei Jingjun of Feixiang, Magistrate Yu Chuzhong of Pu'an, and others to audit military levies in the three cities; they reduced the rolls by one hundred thousand men, and Wan memorialized to disband them.

sentences.zh: 尋授右武衞大將軍，兼檢校晉州刺史，賜爵濟南縣男。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed General of the Right Martial Guards, concurrently acting Governor of Jin Prefecture, and was granted the title Baron of Jinan County.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed General of the Right Martial Guards, concurrently acting governor of Jin Prefecture, and was ennobled as Baron of Jinan County.

sentences.zh: 以年老乞骸骨，拜表訖，不待報而去。

translations.literal: Because of old age he begged to retire on his bones; when he had finished submitting his memorial he did not wait for a reply and left.
translations.idiomatic: On account of old age he requested retirement; having submitted his memorial, he departed without waiting for a reply.

sentences.zh: 優詔加金紫光祿大夫，聽致仕，其祿準品全給。

translations.literal: A gracious edict added the title Grand Master with Purple-Gold Tally, permitted retirement, and his salary according to rank was paid in full.
translations.idiomatic: A gracious edict granted him the title Grand Master with Purple-Gold Tally, permitted his retirement, and ordered his full salary paid according to rank.

sentences.zh: 尋降璽書勞之曰：「卿器局堅正，才識高遠，公忠彰其立身，貞固足以幹事。

translations.literal: Before long an imperial letter with seal was sent down to commend him, saying: 'Your capacity and bearing are firm and upright, your talent and insight lofty and far-reaching; public loyalty shines in how you conduct yourself, and steadfast integrity is sufficient to carry out affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an imperial letter with seal was sent to commend him: 'Your character is firm and upright, your talent and insight lofty; public loyalty marks your conduct, and steadfast integrity suffices to accomplish great affairs.

sentences.zh: 類張騫之出使，同魏絳之和戎。

translations.literal: You resemble Zhang Qian in going on embassy and Wei Jiang in harmonizing with the Rong.
translations.idiomatic: You resemble Zhang Qian in diplomatic missions and Wei Jiang in pacifying the frontier peoples.

sentences.zh: 職綰文武，功申方面，勤於王家，是爲國老。

translations.literal: Your office ties together civil and military affairs; your merit extends to the frontier regions; diligent for the royal house, you are the state's elder.
translations.idiomatic: Your office united civil and military affairs; your achievements extended to the frontier; diligent in the service of the throne, you are a pillar of the state.

sentences.zh: 頃者，顧斯側景，願言勇退，深惜馬援之能，未遂祁奚之請。

translations.literal: Recently, looking back at this declining sun, you expressed the wish to retire boldly; We deeply regret Ma Yuan's ability and have not yet fulfilled Qi Xi's request.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, mindful of advancing age, you expressed the wish to retire; We deeply regret to lose one of Ma Yuan's caliber and have not yet granted Qi Xi's request on your behalf.

sentences.zh: 然章疏頻上，雅懷難奪。

translations.literal: Yet memorial after memorial was submitted, and your refined wish was hard to override.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you submitted memorial after memorial, and your earnest wish could not be denied.

sentences.zh: 今知脫屣歸閑，拂衣高謝，固可以激勵頹俗，儀刑庶僚。

translations.literal: Now knowing that you have cast off your shoes and returned to leisure, brushed your robe and taken high leave, this can indeed rouse and encourage a declining custom and serve as a model for the multitude of officials.
translations.idiomatic: Now that you have cast off office and returned to leisure, brushing off your robes and taking your leave, you will surely inspire a declining age and serve as a model for all officials.

sentences.zh: 永言終始，良可嘉尚。

translations.literal: To speak forever of beginning and end is truly worthy of praise and esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Your constancy from beginning to end is truly admirable.

sentences.zh: 宜善攝養，以介期頤。」

translations.literal: You should well nurture yourself so as to reach the expectancy of a hundred years.'
translations.idiomatic: Take good care of yourself, that you may live to a ripe old age.'

sentences.zh: 未幾，吐蕃寇邊，復召拜左散騎常侍，令與吐蕃分定地界，兼處置十姓降戸。

translations.literal: Before long the Tibetans raided the border; he was again summoned and appointed Left Palace Attendant and ordered to fix the border with Tibet and concurrently to settle the surrendered households of the Ten Surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Tibetans raided the frontier; he was again summoned as Left Palace Attendant and ordered to demarcate the border with Tibet and settle the surrendered households of the Ten Surnames.

sentences.zh: 琬言吐蕃必潛懷叛計，請預支兵十萬於秦、渭等州嚴加防遏。

translations.literal: Wan said the Tibetans would surely secretly harbor plans of rebellion and requested that one hundred thousand troops be advanced in advance in Qin, Wei, and other prefectures for strict defense and blocking.
translations.idiomatic: Wan warned that the Tibetans surely harbored secret plans of rebellion and requested that one hundred thousand troops be stationed in advance in Qin, Wei, and other prefectures for strict defense.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，吐蕃果入寇，竟爲支兵所擊走之。

translations.literal: That winter the Tibetans indeed invaded; in the end they were struck and driven off by the advanced troops.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the Tibetans did invade, but were ultimately driven off by the advance troops he had requested.

sentences.zh: 俄又表請致仕，不許，遷太子賓客。

translations.literal: Before long he again memorialized requesting retirement; this was not granted, and he was transferred to Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he again memorialized requesting retirement; the request was denied, and he was transferred to Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 開元五年，出爲同州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaiyuan he was sent out as Governor of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Kaiyuan he was appointed governor of Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明年卒，年八十餘。

translations.literal: The next year he died, aged over eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year, aged over eighty.

sentences.zh: 畢構畢構，河南偃師人也。

translations.literal: Bi Gou—Bi Gou was a native of Yanshi in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Gou was a native of Yanshi in Henan.

sentences.zh: 父憬，則天時爲司衞少卿。

translations.literal: His father Jing, in the time of Empress Wu, was Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Guards.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jing served as Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Guards under Empress Wu.

sentences.zh: 構少舉進士。

translations.literal: Gou in youth passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Gou passed the jinshi examination in his youth.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，累遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong he was promoted in succession to Attendant Drafting Documents at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shenlong era he rose to Attendant Drafting Documents at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時敬暉等奏請降削武氏諸王，構次當讀表，既聲韻朗暢，兼分析其文句，左右聽者皆歷然可曉。

translations.literal: At that time Jing Hui and others memorialized requesting the demotion and reduction of the Wu princes; Gou was next to read the memorial aloud. Both his tones and rhymes were clear and flowing, and he also analyzed its sentences; all who listened on left and right found it entirely clear and intelligible.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Jing Hui and others memorialized requesting the demotion of the Wu princes; Gou was next to read the memorial aloud. His delivery was clear and resonant, and he explained its sentences as he read; all who heard him found it entirely intelligible.

sentences.zh: 由是武三思惡之，出爲潤州刺史。

translations.literal: From this Wu Sansi hated him, and he was sent out as Governor of Run Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sansi took offense at this and had him demoted to governor of Run Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 累除益州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly removed and appointed Senior Administrator of the Yizhou Metropolitan Area Command.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly appointed senior administrator of the Yizhou metropolitan command.

sentences.zh: 景雲初，召拜左御史大夫，轉陜州刺史，加銀青光祿大夫，封魏縣男。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingyun he was summoned and appointed Left Censor-in-Chief, transferred to Governor of Shan Prefecture, given the additional title Grand Master with Silver-Green Tally, and enfeoffed as Baron of Wei County.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jingyun era he was summoned as Left Censor-in-Chief, transferred to governor of Shan Prefecture, granted the title Grand Master with Silver-Green Tally, and enfeoffed as Baron of Wei County.

sentences.zh: 頃之，復授益州大都督府長史，兼充劍南道按察使。

translations.literal: Before long he was again appointed Senior Administrator of the Yizhou Metropolitan Area Command and concurrently served as Investigation Commissioner of the Jiannan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was again appointed senior administrator of the Yizhou metropolitan command and concurrently served as investigation commissioner of the Jiannan circuit.

sentences.zh: 所歷州府，咸著聲績，在蜀中尤革舊弊，政號清嚴。

translations.literal: In every prefecture and circuit he passed through he won renown for his achievements; in Shu he especially reformed old abuses, and his governance was called pure and stern.
translations.idiomatic: In every prefecture he served he earned renown for his achievements; in Shu he especially reformed longstanding abuses, and his administration was known for its austerity and severity.

sentences.zh: 睿宗聞而善之，璽書勞曰：

translations.literal: Emperor Ruizong heard of this and approved; an imperial letter with seal commended him, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ruizong heard of this and approved; an imperial letter with seal commended him, saying:

sentences.zh: 我國家創開天地，再造黎元，四夷來王，萬邦會至，置州立郡，分職設官。

translations.literal: Our state opened heaven and earth anew and recreated the black-haired people; the four barbarians came to pay homage and the myriad states gathered; prefectures and commanderies were established and offices and officials were apportioned.
translations.idiomatic: Our state opened heaven and earth anew and restored the people; the four quarters came to pay homage and the myriad states gathered; we established prefectures and commanderies and apportioned offices and officials.

sentences.zh: 貞觀、永徽之前，皇猷惟穆；

translations.literal: Before Zhenguan and Yonghui, the imperial plan was solely tranquil;
translations.idiomatic: Before the Zhenguan and Yonghui eras, imperial governance was serene;

sentences.zh: 咸亨、垂拱之後，淳風漸替。

translations.literal: after Xianheng and Chuigong, the pure wind gradually declined.
translations.idiomatic: after Xianheng and Chuigong, honest custom gradually declined.

sentences.zh: 征賦將急，調役頗繁，選吏舉人，涉於浮濫。

translations.literal: Taxes and levies grew pressing, corvée and service duties were quite frequent, and the selection of clerks and recommendees became tainted with superficial excess.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes and levies grew pressing, corvée duties multiplied, and the selection of officials and recommendees became rife with superficial excess.

sentences.zh: 省閣臺寺，罕有公直，茍貪祿秩，以度歳時。

translations.literal: In the ministries, secretariats, censorates, and courts there were rarely men of public integrity; they grasped at salaries and ranks merely to pass the years.
translations.idiomatic: In the ministries, secretariats, censorates, and courts there were rarely men of public integrity; they grasped at salaries and ranks merely to pass the years.

sentences.zh: 中外因循，紀綱弛紊，且無懲革，弊乃滋深。

translations.literal: Within and without all followed precedent; statutes and discipline grew lax and disordered, and with no punishment or reform, abuses only grew deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Within and without all followed precedent; statutes and discipline grew lax, and with no punishment or reform, abuses only deepened.

sentences.zh: 爲官既不擇人，非親即賄；

translations.literal: In appointing officials they did not choose men on merit—if not kin, then bribes;
translations.idiomatic: In appointing officials they did not choose men on merit—if not kin, then bribes;

sentences.zh: 爲法又不按罪，作孽寧逃？

translations.literal: in applying the law they did not punish according to crime—could evildoers escape?
translations.idiomatic: in applying the law they did not punish according to crime—how could evildoers escape?

sentences.zh: 貪殘放手者相仍，清白潔己者斯絶。

translations.literal: The greedy and cruel who let loose their hands followed one after another, while the pure and clean who restrained themselves were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: The greedy and cruel followed one after another, while the pure and self-restrained were cut off entirely.

sentences.zh: 蓋由賞罰不舉，生殺莫行。

translations.literal: This was because rewards and punishments were not carried out and life and death were not enforced.
translations.idiomatic: This was because rewards and punishments were not enforced and the power of life and death was not exercised.

sentences.zh: 更以水旱時乖，邊隅未謐，日損一日，征斂不休，大東小東，杼軸爲怨，就更割剝，何以克堪！

translations.literal: Moreover, because flood and drought came at untimely seasons and the frontiers were not tranquil, day by day things worsened, levies and collections did not cease, great east and small east—the loom and spindle became objects of resentment—and with further stripping and peeling, how could they endure!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, floods and droughts came at untimely seasons and the frontiers were unsettled; day by day conditions worsened, levies never ceased, and the people groaned under the burden of taxation—how could they endure further exactions!

sentences.zh: 昔聞當官，以留犢還珠爲上。

translations.literal: Formerly one heard that in holding office, to leave calves behind and return pearls was highest.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly it was said that the highest standard of office was to leave calves behind and return pearls untouched.

sentences.zh: 今之從職，以充車聯駟爲能。

translations.literal: Today's service in office takes filling carts and linking teams of four as ability.
translations.idiomatic: Today's officials take filling carts and linking teams of horses as the measure of ability.

sentences.zh: 或交結富家，抑棄貧弱；

translations.literal: Some formed ties with wealthy families and oppressed and abandoned the poor and weak;
translations.idiomatic: Some formed ties with wealthy families and oppressed the poor and weak;

sentences.zh: 或矜假典正，樹立腹心。

translations.literal: some put on airs and borrowed the authority of statutes to set up trusted confidants.
translations.idiomatic: some put on airs of legal authority and set up trusted confidants.

sentences.zh: 邑屋之間，囊篋俱委，或地有椿幹梓漆，或家有畜產資財，即被暗通，並從取奪。

translations.literal: Between hamlet and house, bags and boxes were all surrendered; whether the land had toon, catalpa, and lacquer trees or the family had livestock and property, they were secretly communicated and all taken and seized.
translations.idiomatic: In every hamlet and household, bags and boxes were seized; whether the land held valuable timber or the family possessed livestock and property, officials secretly informed on them and seized everything.

sentences.zh: 若有固吝，即因事以繩，粗杖大枷，動傾性命，懷冤抱痛，無所告陳。

translations.literal: If anyone was stubborn and stingy, they used some affair to bind him; with rough staves and great cangues they often endangered lives; bearing injustice and clutching pain, there was nowhere to lodge complaint.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone resisted, they found some pretext to punish him; with rough staves and heavy cangues they often endangered lives, and the victims, bearing injustice and pain, had nowhere to lodge complaint.

sentences.zh: 比差御史委令巡察，或有貴要所囑，未能不避權豪；

translations.literal: Recently censors were dispatched on commission to inspect; some had been entrusted by powerful persons and could not avoid the mighty and great;
translations.idiomatic: Recently censors were dispatched on inspection tours; some had been entrusted by powerful patrons and could not avoid the mighty;

sentences.zh: 或有親故在官，又罕絶於顏面。

translations.literal: some had kin and associates in office and again rarely broke with them face to face.
translations.idiomatic: some had kin and associates in office and rarely broke with them openly.

sentences.zh: 載馳原隰，徒煩出使之名；

translations.literal: They raced across plains and marshes, merely troubling the name of outgoing envoys;
translations.idiomatic: They raced across plains and marshes, merely troubling the name of outgoing envoys;

sentences.zh: 安問狐貍，未見埋車之節。

translations.literal: how could they ask about foxes? The section on burying the carriage was never seen.
translations.idiomatic: they never inquired into wrongdoing, and the section on burying the carriage was never seen.

sentences.zh: 揚清激濁，涇、渭不分；

translations.literal: In raising the clear and stirring the muddy, Jing and Wei were not distinguished;
translations.idiomatic: In raising the clear and stirring the muddy, they did not distinguish Jing from Wei;

sentences.zh: 嫉惡好善，蕭、蘭莫別。

translations.literal: in hating the evil and loving the good, fragrant orchid and stinking eupatorium were not separated.
translations.idiomatic: in hating evil and loving good, they did not distinguish fragrant orchid from stinking eupatorium.

sentences.zh: 官守既其若此，下人豈以聊生。

translations.literal: Since official tenure was like this, how could the people below find ease in living?
translations.idiomatic: When official conduct was like this, how could the common people find ease in living?

sentences.zh: 數年已來，雕殘更甚。

translations.literal: For several years now, devastation has grown worse.
translations.idiomatic: For several years now, devastation has grown worse.

sentences.zh: 卿孤潔獨行，有古人之風，自臨蜀川，弊化頓易。

translations.literal: You are solitary, pure, and walk alone, with the air of ancients; since you took charge of Shu, abuses were suddenly transformed.
translations.idiomatic: You are solitary and upright, with the bearing of the ancients; since you took charge of Shu, abuses were suddenly transformed.

sentences.zh: 覽卿前後執奏，何異破柱求奸？

translations.literal: Reading your memorials before and after, how do they differ from breaking the pillar to seek the traitor?
translations.idiomatic: Reading your memorials before and after, how do they differ from breaking the pillar to seek out wrongdoing?

sentences.zh: 諸使之中，在卿爲最。

translations.literal: Among all commissioners, you are foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Among all commissioners, you are foremost.

sentences.zh: 並能盡節似卿如此，百郡何憂乎不理，萬人何慮乎不安？

translations.literal: If all could exhaust their integrity like you, what worry would the hundred commanderies have of not being governed, what concern would the ten thousand people have of not being secure?
translations.idiomatic: If all could serve with your integrity, what worry would the hundred commanderies have of misgovernment, what concern would the people have of insecurity?

sentences.zh: 卿當益堅，勿爲後顧。

translations.literal: You should grow still firmer and not look back.
translations.idiomatic: You should grow still firmer and not look back.

sentences.zh: 朕嘉卿直道，今賜袍帶並衣一副。

translations.literal: We commend your upright way and now bestow one set of robe, belt, and garments.
translations.idiomatic: We commend your upright conduct and now bestow one set of robe, belt, and garments.

sentences.zh: 尋拜戸部尚書，轉吏部尚書，並遙領益州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Minister of Revenue, transferred to Minister of Personnel, and concurrently held the distant post of Senior Administrator of the Yizhou Metropolitan Area Command.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Minister of Revenue, then transferred to Minister of Personnel, while retaining the distant post of senior administrator of the Yizhou metropolitan command.

sentences.zh: 玄宗即位，累拜河南尹，遷戸部尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong took the throne, Gou was repeatedly appointed Intendant of Henan and promoted to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong acceded to the throne, Gou was repeatedly appointed Intendant of Henan and promoted to Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 開元四年，遇疾，上手疏醫方以賜之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaiyuan he fell ill; the emperor personally wrote out a medical prescription and bestowed it on him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaiyuan he fell ill; the emperor personally wrote out a medical prescription and bestowed it on him.

sentences.zh: 時議戸部尚書爲凶官，遽改授太子詹事，冀其有瘳。

translations.literal: At the time it was said that Minister of Revenue was an unlucky office; he was hastily reassigned as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, in hope that he might recover.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Minister of Revenue was considered an unlucky office; he was hastily reassigned as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent in hope that he might recover.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，贈黃門監，謚曰景。

translations.literal: Before long he died; he was posthumously given the office of Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat, with the posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward and was posthumously appointed Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat with the posthumous title Jing.

sentences.zh: 構初喪繼母時，有二妹在繈褓，親加鞠養，咸得成立。

translations.literal: When Gou first mourned his stepmother, he had two younger sisters in swaddling clothes; he personally nursed and raised them, and all were able to grow up.
translations.idiomatic: When Gou first mourned his stepmother, he had two infant sisters; he personally nursed and raised them, and both grew to maturity.

sentences.zh: 及構卒，二妹號絶久之，以撫育恩，遂制三年之服。

translations.literal: When Gou died, the two sisters wailed until they were exhausted for a long time; because of the grace of his nurturing, they thereupon observed three years of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When Gou died, the two sisters mourned him at length and, out of gratitude for his nurturing, observed three years of mourning for him.

sentences.zh: 其弟栩亦甚哀毀，並爲當時所稱。

translations.literal: His younger brother Xu was also deeply grief-stricken and self-impoverished; both were praised by their time.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xu was also deeply grief-stricken; both were praised by their contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 栩官至荊州司馬。

translations.literal: Xu reached the office of Senior Administrator of Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xu rose to senior administrator of Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 蘇珦蘇珦，雍州藍田人。

translations.literal: Su Xuan—Su Xuan was a native of Lantian in Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Su Xuan was a native of Lantian in Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明經舉，累授鄠縣尉。

translations.literal: He passed the Mingjing examination and was repeatedly appointed magistrate of Hu County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Classics examination and was repeatedly appointed magistrate of Hu County.

sentences.zh: 雍州長史李義琰召而謂曰：「鄠縣本多訴訟，近日遂絶，訪問果由明公爲其疏理。」

translations.literal: Yong Prefecture Senior Administrator Li Yiyan summoned him and said: 'Hu County originally had many lawsuits; recently they have ceased entirely. On inquiry it is indeed because you, sir, have cleared and ordered them for the people.'
translations.idiomatic: Yong Prefecture Senior Administrator Li Yiyan summoned him and said: 'Hu County originally had many lawsuits; recently they have ceased entirely. On inquiry I find it is indeed because you have cleared and ordered them.'

sentences.zh: 因顧指廳事曰：「此座即明公座也，但恨非遲暮所見耳。」

translations.literal: He thereupon turned and pointed at the hall seat, saying: 'This seat is your seat, sir; I only regret it was not seen in my late years.'
translations.idiomatic: He then turned and pointed at the seat in the hall, saying: 'This seat is yours, sir; I only regret I did not see you in office sooner.'

sentences.zh: 垂拱初，拜右臺監察御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chuigong he was appointed Investigating Censor of the Right Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chuigong era he was appointed Investigating Censor of the Right Bureau.

sentences.zh: 時則天將誅韓、魯等諸王，使珦按其密狀，珦訊問皆無征驗。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Wu was about to execute the princes Han, Lu, and others; she had Xuan investigate their secret charges, and in his interrogation nothing was verified.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Empress Wu was about to execute the Han, Lu, and other princes; she had Xuan investigate their secret charges, but his interrogation found no evidence.

sentences.zh: 或誣告珦與韓、魯等同情，則天召見詰問，珦抗議不回。

translations.literal: Someone falsely accused Xuan of sympathizing with Han, Lu, and the others; Empress Wu summoned him for questioning, and Xuan protested firmly without yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Someone falsely accused Xuan of sympathizing with the Han and Lu princes; Empress Wu summoned him for questioning, and Xuan protested firmly without yielding.

sentences.zh: 則天不悅，曰：「卿大雅之士，朕當別有驅使，此獄不假卿也。」

translations.literal: Empress Wu was displeased and said: 'You are a man of great refinement; We shall have other employment for you—this case does not require you.'
translations.idiomatic: The empress was displeased and said: 'You are a man of great refinement; I shall have other employment for you—this case does not require you.'

sentences.zh: 遂令珦於河西監軍。

translations.literal: She thereupon ordered Xuan to supervise the army in Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: She thereupon ordered Xuan to supervise the army in Hexi.

sentences.zh: 五遷右司郎中。

translations.literal: After five promotions he became Director of the Right Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: After five promotions he became Director of the Right Bureau.

sentences.zh: 時御史王弘義托附來俊臣，構陷無罪，朝廷疾之。

translations.literal: At that time Censor Wang Hongyi relied on Lai Junchen and framed the innocent; the court detested him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Censor Wang Hongyi relied on Lai Junchen and framed the innocent; the court detested him.

sentences.zh: 嘗受詔於虢州采木，役使不節，丁夫多死，珦按奏其事，弘義竟以坐黜。

translations.literal: He had once received an edict to gather timber in Guo Prefecture; his use of labor was unrestrained and many corvée laborers died; Xuan investigated and memorialized the matter, and Hongyi was ultimately dismissed for the offense.
translations.idiomatic: He had once received an edict to gather timber in Guo Prefecture; his use of labor was unrestrained and many corvée laborers died; Xuan investigated and memorialized the matter, and Hongyi was ultimately dismissed.

sentences.zh: 珦尋遷給事中，累授左肅政臺御史大夫。

translations.literal: Xuan was soon promoted to Attendant Drafting Documents and repeatedly given the post of Censor-in-Chief of the Left Bureau for Rectifying Governance.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was soon promoted to Attendant Drafting Documents and eventually appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Left Bureau for Rectifying Governance.

sentences.zh: 時有詔白司馬阪營大像，糜費巨億，珦以妨農，上疏切諫，則天納焉。

translations.literal: At that time there was an edict to build a great image at Baima Slope, wasting hundreds of millions; Xuan, on the ground that it hindered agriculture, submitted a forthright memorial remonstrating, and Empress Wu accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there was an edict to build a great image at Baima Slope, wasting hundreds of millions; Xuan memorialized that it would hinder agriculture, and the empress accepted his remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，武三思擅權，韋月將告三思將有逆謀，反爲三思所構，中宗令斬之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, Wu Sansi monopolized power; Wei Yuejiang reported that Sansi would have a treasonous plot, but on the contrary was framed by Sansi, and Emperor Zhongzong ordered him beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shenlong era Wu Sansi held unchecked power; Wei Yuejiang reported that Sansi was plotting treason, but was instead framed by Sansi, and Emperor Zhongzong ordered his execution.

sentences.zh: 珦奏非時不可行刑，由是忤三思旨，轉爲右御史大夫。

translations.literal: Xuan memorialized that it was not the proper season for execution; thereby he offended Sansi's intent and was transferred to Right Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan memorialized that it was not the proper season for execution; thereby he offended Sansi and was transferred to Right Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 尋出爲岐州刺史，復爲右臺大夫。

translations.literal: Before long he was sent out as Governor of Qi Prefecture, then again became Censor-in-Chief of the Right Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was sent out as governor of Qi Prefecture, then again became Censor-in-Chief of the Right Bureau.

sentences.zh: 會節湣太子敗，詔珦窮其黨與。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince Jiemin was defeated, an edict ordered Xuan to exhaustively pursue his faction and associates.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Jiemin was defeated, an edict ordered Xuan to pursue his faction and associates exhaustively.

sentences.zh: 時睿宗在籓，爲得罪者所引，珦因辯析事狀，密奏以保持之。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Ruizong was in his princely fief and was implicated by those who had offended; Xuan thereupon analyzed the facts of the case and submitted a secret memorial to preserve him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Ruizong was in his princely fief and was implicated by the accused; Xuan analyzed the facts of the case and submitted a secret memorial to protect him.

sentences.zh: 中宗意解，因是多所原免，擢珦爲戸部尚書，賜爵河內郡公。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhongzong's mind was eased, and thereby many were pardoned and exempted; Xuan was promoted to Minister of Revenue and granted the title Duke of Henei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhongzong's mind was eased, and many were pardoned as a result; Xuan was promoted to Minister of Revenue and enfeoffed as Duke of Henei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 尋授太子賓客、檢校詹事，以年老致仕。

translations.literal: Before long he was given the posts of Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Acting Grand Mentor, and retired on account of old age.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Acting Grand Mentor, then retired on account of old age.

sentences.zh: 開元三年卒，年八十一，贈兗州都督，謚曰文。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaiyuan he died, aged eighty-one; he was posthumously given the office of Area Commander of Yan Prefecture, with the posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Kaiyuan, aged eighty-one; he was posthumously appointed Area Commander of Yan Prefecture with the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 子晉，亦知名。

translations.literal: His son Jin was also well known.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jin was also well known.

sentences.zh: 珦子 晉晉，數歳能屬文，作《八卦論》，吏部侍郎房穎敘、秘書少監王紹宗見而賞嘆曰：「此後來王粲也。」

translations.literal: Xuan's son Jin—Jin, at several years of age could compose prose; he wrote 'Treatise on the Eight Trigrams.' Vice Minister of Personnel Fang Yingxu and Vice Director of the Secretariat Wang Shaozong saw it and praised in admiration: 'This is a Wang Can to come.'
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's son Jin, while still a child, could compose prose and wrote Treatise on the Eight Trigrams. Vice Minister of Personnel Fang Yingxu and Vice Director of the Secretariat Wang Shaozong read it and exclaimed in admiration: 'Here is a Wang Can in the making.'

sentences.zh: 弱冠舉進士，又應大禮舉，皆居上第。

translations.literal: In his weak-crown years he passed the jinshi examination and also responded to the great ritual examination; in both he ranked in the upper tier.
translations.idiomatic: In his early twenties he passed the jinshi examination and also the great ritual examination; in both he ranked at the top.

sentences.zh: 先天中，累遷中書舍人，兼崇文館學士。

translations.literal: During Xiantian he was promoted in succession to Attendant Drafting Documents at the Secretariat and concurrently Academician of the Chongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiantian era he rose to Attendant Drafting Documents at the Secretariat and concurrently served as Academician of the Chongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 玄宗監國，毎有制命，皆令晉及賈曾爲之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong supervised the state, whenever there were edicts and orders, Jin and Jia Zeng were both ordered to draft them.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong served as regent, whenever there were edicts and orders, Jin and Jia Zeng were ordered to draft them.

sentences.zh: 晉亦數進讜言，深見嘉納。

translations.literal: Jin also repeatedly submitted forthright words and was deeply commended and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Jin also repeatedly submitted forthright counsel and was deeply commended.

sentences.zh: 俄出爲泗州刺史，以父老乞辭職歸侍，許之。

translations.literal: Before long he was sent out as Governor of Si Prefecture; because his father was old he begged to resign and return to serve him, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed governor of Si Prefecture; because his father was elderly he begged to resign and return home to serve him, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 父卒後，歷戸部侍郎，襲爵河內郡公。

translations.literal: After his father's death he served as Vice Minister of Revenue and inherited the title Duke of Henei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he served as Vice Minister of Revenue and inherited the title Duke of Henei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 開元十四年，遷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Kaiyuan he was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Kaiyuan he was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時開府宋璟兼尚書事，晉及齊澣遞於京都知選事，既糊名考判，晉獨多賞拔，甚得當時之譽。

translations.literal: At that time Song Jing of the Kaifu rank concurrently handled Secretariat affairs; Jin and Qi Huan took turns in the capital managing selection affairs; after the names were sealed for examination and judgment, Jin alone made many commendations and promotions and greatly won the praise of the time.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Song Jing of the Kaifu rank concurrently handled Secretariat affairs; Jin and Qi Huan took turns managing selection affairs in the capital; after names were sealed for examination, Jin alone made many commendations and promotions and won great acclaim.

sentences.zh: 俄而侍中裴光庭知尚書事，毎遇官應批退者，但對眾披簿，以硃筆點頭而已。

translations.literal: Before long Palace Attendant Pei Guangting handled Secretariat affairs; whenever an official should have been rejected, he merely opened the register before the assembly and with a vermilion brush made a dot—that was all.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Palace Attendant Pei Guangting handled Secretariat affairs; whenever an official should have been rejected, he merely opened the register before the assembly and marked it with a vermilion dot—that was all.

sentences.zh: 晉遂榜選院云：「門下點頭者，更引註擬。」

translations.literal: Jin thereupon posted a notice at the Selection Court saying: 'Those whom the Secretariat has dotted must be brought forward again for annotation and nomination.'
translations.idiomatic: Jin thereupon posted a notice at the Selection Court: 'Those whom the Secretariat has dotted must be brought forward again for review and nomination.'

sentences.zh: 光庭以爲侮己，甚不悅，遂出爲汝州刺史。

translations.literal: Guangting took this as an insult to himself and was greatly displeased; Jin was thereupon sent out as Governor of Ru Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Guangting took this as an insult and was greatly displeased; Jin was thereupon demoted to governor of Ru Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三遷魏州刺史，加銀青光祿大夫，入爲太子左庶子。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became Governor of Wei Prefecture, was given the additional title Grand Master with Silver-Green Tally, and entered the capital as Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he became governor of Wei Prefecture, was granted the title Grand Master with Silver-Green Tally, and entered the capital as Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 二十二年卒，年五十九。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he died, aged fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-second year, aged fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 初，晉與洛陽人張循之、仲之兄弟友善，循之等並以學業著名。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jin was on friendly terms with Zhang Xunzhi and the brothers Zhongzhi of Luoyang; Xunzhi and the others were all famed for their learning.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Jin was on friendly terms with Zhang Xunzhi and the brothers Zhongzhi of Luoyang; Xunzhi and the others were all famed for their scholarship.

sentences.zh: 循之，則天時上書忤旨被誅。

translations.literal: Xunzhi, in the time of Empress Wu, submitted a memorial that offended the intent and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Xunzhi, under Empress Wu, submitted a memorial that offended the throne and was executed.

sentences.zh: 仲之，神龍中謀殺武三思，爲友人宋之愻所發，下獄死。

translations.literal: Zhongzhi, during Shenlong plotted to kill Wu Sansi; he was exposed by his friend Song Zhisun, was imprisoned, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzhi, during the Shenlong era plotted to kill Wu Sansi; he was exposed by his friend Song Zhisun, imprisoned, and died.

sentences.zh: 晉厚撫仲之子漸，有如己子，教之書記，爲營婚宦。

translations.literal: Jin generously nurtured Zhongzhi's son Jian as if he were his own son, taught him secretarial writing, and arranged marriage and office for him.
translations.idiomatic: Jin generously nurtured Zhongzhi's son Jian as if he were his own son, taught him secretarial writing, and arranged marriage and office for him.

sentences.zh: 及晉卒，漸制猶子之服，時人甚以此稱之。

translations.literal: When Jin died, Jian observed the mourning garments of a nephew-son; people of the time greatly praised this.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin died, Jian observed the mourning garments of a nephew; contemporaries greatly praised this.

sentences.zh: 鄭惟忠鄭惟忠，宋州宋城人也。

translations.literal: Zheng Weizhong—Zheng Weizhong was a native of Songcheng in Song Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Weizhong was a native of Songcheng in Song Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳中，進士舉，授井陘尉，轉湯陰尉。

translations.literal: During Yifeng he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed magistrate of Jingxing, then transferred to magistrate of Tangyin.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yifeng era he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed magistrate of Jingxing, then transferred to magistrate of Tangyin.

sentences.zh: 天授中，應舉召見，則天臨軒問諸舉人：「何者爲忠？」

translations.literal: During Tianshou he responded to the examination summons and audience; Empress Wu, facing the hall, asked the examinees: 'What is loyalty?'
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianshou era he was summoned for examination and audience; Empress Wu, facing the hall, asked the examinees: 'What is loyalty?'

sentences.zh: 諸人對不稱旨。

translations.literal: The various men's answers did not please the intent.
translations.idiomatic: The various answers did not please her.

sentences.zh: 惟忠對曰：「臣聞忠者，外揚君之美，內匡君之惡。」

translations.literal: Weizhong answered: 'Your servant has heard that loyalty is outwardly to display the ruler's excellence and inwardly to correct the ruler's evil.'
translations.idiomatic: Weizhong answered: 'Your servant has heard that loyalty means outwardly to display the ruler's excellence and inwardly to correct the ruler's faults.'

sentences.zh: 則天曰：「善。」

translations.literal: Empress Wu said: 'Good.'
translations.idiomatic: The empress said: 'Good.'

sentences.zh: 授左司禦率府胄曹參軍，累遷水部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Aide in the Left Bureau of the Imperial Guard Command and was promoted in succession to Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed aide in the Left Bureau of the Imperial Guard Command and rose to Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 則天幸長安，惟忠待制引見，則天謂曰：「朕識卿，前於東都言『忠臣外揚君之美，內匡君之惡』，至今不忘。」

translations.literal: When Empress Wu visited Chang'an, Weizhong waited on duty for audience and introduction; Empress Wu said: 'We recognize you; formerly in the eastern capital you said that a loyal minister outwardly displays the ruler's excellence and inwardly corrects the ruler's evil—we have not forgotten to this day.'
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wu visited Chang'an, Weizhong waited on duty for audience; the empress said: 'I recognize you; formerly in the eastern capital you said that a loyal minister outwardly displays the ruler's excellence and inwardly corrects the ruler's faults—I have not forgotten to this day.'

sentences.zh: 尋加朝散大夫，再遷鳳閣舍人。

translations.literal: Before long he was given the title Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and was twice promoted to Attendant of the Phoenix Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was granted the title Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and was twice promoted to Attendant of the Phoenix Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，甚敬重之，擢拜黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhongzong took the throne, he greatly respected Weizhong and promoted him to Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong acceded to the throne, he greatly respected Weizhong and promoted him to Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時議請禁嶺南首領家畜兵器，惟忠曰：「夫爲政不可革以習俗，且《吳都賦》云：『家有鶴膝，戸有犀渠。』

translations.literal: At the time it was proposed to forbid the chieftains of Lingnan from keeping weapons in their households; Weizhong said: 'In governing one cannot change things according to custom, and moreover the Rhapsody on the Wu Capital says: "In every house there are crane-knee crossbows; in every door there are rhinoceros-hide shields.
translations.idiomatic: At the time it was proposed to forbid the chieftains of Lingnan from keeping weapons in their households; Weizhong said: 'In governing one cannot simply overturn custom, and moreover the Rhapsody on the Wu Capital says: "In every house there are crane-knee crossbows; in every door there are rhinoceros-hide shields.

sentences.zh: 如或禁之，豈無驚擾耶？」

translations.literal: If one were to forbid this, would there not be alarm and disturbance?"
translations.idiomatic: If we were to forbid this, would there not be alarm and disturbance?"

sentences.zh: 遂寢。

translations.literal: Thereupon the matter was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the proposal was shelved.

sentences.zh: 無何，守大理卿。

translations.literal: Before long he served as Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward he was appointed Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 節湣太子與將軍李多祚等舉兵誅武三思，事變伏誅。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Jiemin together with General Li Duozuo and others raised troops to execute Wu Sansi; the plot failed and they were put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Jiemin and General Li Duozuo and others raised an army to kill Wu Sansi, but the plot failed and they were executed.

sentences.zh: 其詿誤守門者並配流，將行，有韋氏黨與密奏請盡誅之。

translations.literal: Those gatekeepers who had been misled were all sentenced to exile; as they were about to depart, followers of the Wei clan secretly memorialized requesting that all be executed.
translations.idiomatic: The gatekeepers who had been drawn into the affair were all sentenced to banishment; just as they were about to leave, members of the Wei faction secretly petitioned the throne to have them all put to death.

sentences.zh: 中宗令推斷，惟忠奏曰：「今大獄始決，人心未寧，若更改推，必遞相驚恐，則反側之子，無由自安。」

translations.literal: Emperor Zhongzong ordered a review of the verdict; Weizhong memorialized, saying: "The great case has only just been decided and the people's hearts are not yet settled; if the verdict is changed anew, fear will surely spread from one to another, and those who waver will have no way to find peace."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhongzong ordered the case reconsidered, but Weizhong submitted a memorial saying: "This major trial has only just been concluded and the public is still unsettled; if we reopen the judgment, alarm will spread from one person to the next, and those who already feel insecure will have no way to rest easy."

sentences.zh: 敕令百司議，遂依舊斷，所全者甚多。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the hundred offices to discuss the matter, and in the end the original verdict was upheld; many lives were spared.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered all departments to deliberate, and the original sentences were upheld; a great many people were spared.

sentences.zh: 俄拜御史大夫，持節賑給河北道，仍黜陟牧宰。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Censor-in-Chief, bearing credentials to provide famine relief in the Hebei Circuit, and also to promote or demote the prefectural governors.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made Censor-in-Chief, sent with imperial credentials to distribute relief in the Hebei region while also evaluating and appointing or removing local prefects.

sentences.zh: 還，敷奏稱旨，加銀青光祿大夫，封滎陽縣男。

translations.literal: On his return he reported to the throne in a manner that pleased the emperor, and was given the additional title Grand Master with Silver-Green Tally and enfeoffed as Baron of Xingyang County.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned, his report to the throne pleased the emperor, who promoted him to Grand Master with Silver-Green Tally and enfeoffed him as Baron of Xingyang County.

sentences.zh: 開元初，爲禮部尚書，轉太子賓客。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Kaiyuan era he became Minister of Rites, then was transferred to Senior Mentor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyuan reign he served as Minister of Rites, then was transferred to Senior Mentor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 十年卒，贈太子少保。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he died and was posthumously awarded the title Junior Guardian of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth year of the era and was posthumously honored as Junior Guardian of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 王志愔王志愔，博州聊城人也。

translations.literal: Wang Zhiyin was a native of Liaocheng in Bo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhiyin was a native of Liaocheng in Bo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少以進士擢第。

translations.literal: In youth he passed the Jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he passed the Jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 神龍年，累除左臺御史，加朝散大夫。

translations.literal: In the Shenlong era he was repeatedly promoted to Left Censor, with the added title Grand Master for Court Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenlong era he rose through successive appointments to Left Censor and received the added title Grand Master for Court Discussion.

sentences.zh: 執法剛正，百僚畏憚，時人呼爲「皁雕」，言其顧瞻人吏，如雕鶚之視燕雀也。

translations.literal: In enforcing the law he was upright and strict; the hundred officials feared him, and people of the time called him the "Black Eagle," meaning that when he looked upon officials and clerks it was as an eagle or hawk eyeing sparrows and finches.
translations.idiomatic: He enforced the law with uncompromising firmness, and the officials all feared him; contemporaries called him the "Black Eagle," saying that when he fixed his gaze on officials and clerks it was like an eagle or hawk watching sparrows.

sentences.zh: 尋遷大理正，嘗奏言：「法令者，人之堤防，堤防不立，則人無所禁。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to be Director of Cases in the Court of Judicial Review; he once memorialized, saying: "Laws and ordinances are the dikes and ramparts of men; if dikes and ramparts are not established, then men have nothing to restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Director of Cases at the Court of Judicial Review and once submitted a memorial saying: "Law is the dyke that holds human conduct in check; if the dyke is not built, people have nothing to hold them back.

sentences.zh: 竊見大理官僚，多不奉法，以縱罪爲寬恕，以守文爲苛刻。

translations.literal: I have observed that many officials of the Court of Judicial Review do not uphold the law, taking the release of the guilty as leniency and adherence to the letter of the law as harshness.
translations.idiomatic: I have seen that many officials in the Court of Judicial Review fail to follow the law, treating the release of offenders as mercy and strict adherence to the statutes as cruelty.

sentences.zh: 臣濫執刑典，實恐爲眾所謗。」

translations.literal: I have undeservedly been entrusted with the penal code, and truly fear being slandered by the multitude."
translations.idiomatic: I hold the office of punishment only by unearned appointment, and I truly fear being condemned by my colleagues."

sentences.zh: 遂表上所著《應正論》以見誌，其詞曰：

translations.literal: He thereupon submitted a memorial presenting his treatise "On Responding to Uprightness" to express his intent; its words say:
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial along with his treatise "On Responding to Uprightness" to make his views known. It reads:

sentences.zh: 嘗讀《易》至「萃，利見大人，亨，聚以正也。

translations.literal: I once read in the Book of Changes down to [the hexagram] Cui: "Beneficial to see the great man. Success. Gathering in accordance with the correct.
translations.idiomatic: Once, reading the Book of Changes, I came to the hexagram Cui: "It is beneficial to see the great man. Success. Gathering together in the right way.

sentences.zh: 六二，引吉無咎。」

translations.literal: Six in the second place: "Being led brings good fortune without blame."
translations.idiomatic: The second line reads: "Being led brings good fortune without blame."

sentences.zh: 註曰：「居萃之時，體柔當位。
