translations.literal: The commentary says: "In the time of gathering, with a yielding nature and occupying the proper position.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary explains: "In a time of gathering, one is yielding by nature yet holds the proper place.

sentences.zh: 處《坤》之中，己獨處正。

translations.literal: Situated within Kun, yet alone maintaining uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Standing within Kun, one alone keeps to what is upright.

sentences.zh: 異操而聚，獨正者危，未能變體，以遠於害。

translations.literal: Different in conduct while gathering together—the one who alone is upright is in peril; unable to alter his substance, he has not yet kept far from harm.
translations.idiomatic: When people of different conduct assemble, the one who alone remains upright is in danger; unable to change his nature, he has not yet escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 故必見引，然後乃吉而無咎。」

translations.literal: Therefore one must be led and welcomed, and only then is there good fortune without blame."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore one must be welcomed and guided before good fortune comes without blame."

sentences.zh: 王肅曰：「六二與九五相應，俱履貞正。

translations.literal: Wang Su said: "The second line and the fifth line respond to each other, both treading in steadfast uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su said: "The second line and the fifth line correspond to each other, both acting in firm uprightness.

sentences.zh: 引由迎也，爲吉所迎，何咎之有？」

translations.literal: Being led means being welcomed; welcomed by what is auspicious—what blame could there be?"
translations.idiomatic: To be led is to be welcomed; welcomed by what is auspicious—what fault could there be?"

sentences.zh: 未嘗不輟書而嘆曰：「居中履正，事之常體，見引無咎，道亦宜然。

translations.literal: I never failed to lay down the book and sigh, saying: "To hold the center and tread the correct path is the constant norm of affairs; to be led and welcomed without blame—the Way ought to be so as well.
translations.idiomatic: I could not help closing the book and sighing: "To hold the center and walk the upright path is the ordinary way of things; to be welcomed and guided without blame—the Way should work like that too.

sentences.zh: 有客聞而惑之，因謂僕曰：今主上文明，域中理定，君累司典憲，不務和同。

translations.literal: A visitor who heard this was perplexed and thereupon said to me: "The present sovereign is enlightened; order within the realm is settled; you repeatedly hold office over the penal statutes, yet do not strive for harmony and agreement.
translations.idiomatic: A guest who heard this was puzzled and said to me: "The emperor today is enlightened, and order is settled throughout the realm; you have repeatedly held judicial office, yet you do not seek harmony and agreement.

sentences.zh: 處正之志雖存，見引之吉誰應？

translations.literal: Though the will to maintain uprightness remains, who will respond to the good fortune of being led and welcomed?
translations.idiomatic: You may still wish to stand upright, but who will answer with the good fortune of welcome and guidance?

sentences.zh: 行之不已，余竊懼焉。

translations.literal: If you continue this without cease, I privately fear for you."
translations.idiomatic: If you keep on this way, I am privately afraid for you."

sentences.zh: 僕斂襟降階揖而謝曰：補遺闕於袞職，用忠讜爲己任，以蒙養正，見引獲吉，應此道也，仁何遠哉！

translations.literal: I straightened my robe, descended the steps, bowed with joined hands and replied: "To repair omissions and fill gaps in one's imperial duties, to take loyal remonstrance as one's charge—to be nurtured in uprightness and, being led and welcomed, obtain good fortune—this responds to the Way; how far can benevolence be!
translations.idiomatic: I straightened my robe, stepped down, bowed, and answered: "To remedy what is missing in one's official duty and to take loyal remonstrance as one's task—to be nurtured in uprightness and, through welcome and guidance, gain good fortune—this is what the Way calls for; how distant can humaneness be!

sentences.zh: 昔咎繇謨虞，登朝作士，設教理物，開訓成務。

translations.literal: In antiquity Gao Yao counseled at Yu's court, entered court as Minister of Crime, established teachings to govern things, and opened instruction to accomplish tasks.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Gao Yao advised the court of Yu, entered government as Minister of Crime, set up teaching to order affairs, and opened instruction to complete the work of governance.

sentences.zh: 是以五流有宅，五宅三居，怙終賊刑，刑故無小。

translations.literal: Hence the five punishments of exile had their places, the five places had three residences; those who persisted to the end faced the extreme penalty, and in punishing old offenses nothing was considered small.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the five degrees of banishment each had their proper place, and the five places had three levels of residence; those who persisted in wrongdoing faced the harshest punishment, and even old offenses were not treated lightly.

sentences.zh: 於是舜美其事曰：「汝明於五刑，以弼五教，期於予理，刑期於無刑，人協於中，時乃功，懋哉！」

translations.literal: Thereupon Shun praised this work, saying: "You are clear about the five punishments, to assist the five teachings, aiming at my good governance; punishment aims at there being no punishment; the people harmonize in the mean—timely is this achievement; exert yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: Then Shun praised his work, saying: "You are clear in the five punishments and thereby support the five teachings; you aim at good order under me, and punishment aims at the day when punishment is no longer needed; the people are brought into harmony—this is timely achievement; press on!"

sentences.zh: 故孔子嘆其政曰：「舜舉咎繇，不仁者遠。」

translations.literal: Therefore Confucius sighed in admiration of this governance, saying: "When Shun raised up Gao Yao, the unbenevolent kept their distance."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius admired this governance and said: "When Shun elevated Gao Yao, the unworthy withdrew of themselves."

sentences.zh: 此非明辟執法，大人見引之應乎？

translations.literal: Is this not the response of the enlightened sovereign enforcing the law and the great man being led and welcomed?
translations.idiomatic: Is this not the very response of an enlightened ruler enforcing the law and a great man being welcomed and guided?

sentences.zh: 季孫行父之事君也，舉竊寶之愆，黜授邑之賞，明善惡而糾慝，議僭賞以塞違。

translations.literal: In serving his lord, Ji Sun Xingfu exposed the crime of stealing a jewel, dismissed a reward of granted fief, clarified good and evil and corrected wickedness, and debated excessive rewards to block transgression.
translations.idiomatic: In serving his ruler, Jisun Xingfu reported the crime of stealing a treasure, rejected an improper grant of fief, distinguished good from evil and corrected wrongdoing, and challenged excessive rewards in order to stop misconduct.

sentences.zh: 在虞舜之功，居二十之一，主司得行其道，時君不以爲嫌，此非己獨處正，應正而無咎。

translations.literal: Among the achievements of Shun of Yu, this ranks as one of twenty; the responsible official was able to carry out his way, and the ruler of the time did not take it amiss—is this not standing alone in uprightness and responding to what is correct without blame?
translations.idiomatic: Among the achievements of Emperor Shun, this counted as one in twenty; the official in charge was able to act according to his principles, and the ruler did not resent it—is this not standing alone in uprightness and answering what is correct without blame?

sentences.zh: 觀魚於棠，臧伯正色；

translations.literal: When [Duke Zhuang] watched fish at Tang, Zang Bo showed stern countenance;
translations.idiomatic: When the duke went to Tang to watch fish, Zang Bo rebuked him sternly;

sentences.zh: 賂鼎在廟，哀伯抗詞。

translations.literal: when a bribed tripod was in the ancestral temple, Ai Bo spoke out in opposition.
translations.idiomatic: when a bribed bronze vessel stood in the ancestral temple, Ai Bo spoke out against it.

sentences.zh: 言者得盡其忠，聞之不加其罪。

translations.literal: Those who spoke could fully exhaust their loyalty, and the one who heard did not add punishment for it.
translations.idiomatic: Those who remonstrated could speak their full loyalty, and the ruler who heard them did not punish them for it.

sentences.zh: 故《春秋》稱臧氏之正，曰：「積善之家，必有餘慶。」

translations.literal: Therefore the Spring and Autumn Annals praised the uprightness of the Zang clan, saying: "A family that accumulates goodness is sure to have surplus blessing."
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals therefore praised the uprightness of the Zang house, saying: "A family that accumulates goodness will surely have blessing left over."

sentences.zh: 此非異操而聚，引吉之所致乎？

translations.literal: Is this not the effect of gathering though different in conduct, and being led to good fortune?
translations.idiomatic: Is this not what comes of gathering together while differing in conduct, and being led to good fortune?

sentences.zh: 魏絳理直，晉侯乃復其位；

translations.literal: Wei Jiang's reasoning was straight, and Duke Wu of Jin thereupon restored his position;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jiang's argument was just, and Duke Wu of Jin then restored him to office;

sentences.zh: 邾人辭順，趙盾不伐其國。

translations.literal: the people of Zhu spoke deferentially, and Zhao Dun did not attack their state.
translations.idiomatic: the people of Zhu spoke with proper deference, and Zhao Dun did not invade their state.

sentences.zh: 此非正體未變，爲吉所迎者乎？

translations.literal: Is this not a case where the upright substance was unchanged and one was welcomed by what was auspicious?
translations.idiomatic: Is this not a case in which uprightness remained unchanged and one was welcomed by what was auspicious?

sentences.zh: 夫在上垂拱，臣下守制，若正應乎上，乃引吉於下。

translations.literal: When the ruler above sits in repose and ministers below observe the statutes, if uprightness responds to those above, then below there is the good fortune of being led and welcomed.
translations.idiomatic: When the sovereign above rules with folded hands and ministers below keep to the law, if uprightness answers those above, then below there is the good fortune of welcome and guidance.

sentences.zh: 而中士聞道，若存若亡，交戰於譎正之門，懷疑乎語默之境，懼獨正之莫引，忘此正之必亨。

translations.literal: Yet when men of the middle rank hear the Way, it seems to exist and not to exist; they do battle at the gate between cunning and uprightness, stand in doubt between speech and silence, fear that standing alone in uprightness will not be welcomed, and forget that this uprightness must bring success.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when ordinary officers hear the Way, it seems present one moment and gone the next; they struggle at the threshold between cunning and uprightness, hesitate between speaking and keeping silent, fear that standing alone in uprightness will win no welcome, and forget that such uprightness must succeed.

sentences.zh: 籲嗟乎！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 行己立身，居正踐義，其動也直，其正也方。

translations.literal: Conduct yourself and establish your person, dwell in uprightness and practice righteousness—your movement is straight, your uprightness square.
translations.idiomatic: In how you conduct yourself and establish your character, dwell in uprightness and act in righteousness—your action is straight, your standard square.

sentences.zh: 維正直而是與，何往而非攸利。

translations.literal: Only align with what is upright and correct—where could you go that would not be wholly to your benefit?
translations.idiomatic: Keep only to what is upright and correct, and where could you go that would not be wholly to your benefit?

sentences.zh: 何以明之？

translations.literal: How may this be made clear?
translations.idiomatic: How can this be shown?

sentences.zh: 《坤》六二：「直方大，不習無不利。」

translations.literal: Kun, six in the second place: "Straight, square, and great; without repeated practice, nothing is not beneficial."
translations.idiomatic: The second line of Kun says: "Straight, square, and great; without deliberate effort, nothing is unfavorable."

sentences.zh: 《文言》曰：「直其正也，方其義也，君子敬以直內，義以方外。

translations.literal: The Remarks on the Text say: "Straightness is its uprightness; squareness is its righteousness; the noble person uses reverence to be straight within and righteousness to be square without.
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary on the Text says: "Straightness is its rectitude; squareness is its duty; the noble person uses reverence to make himself straight within and righteousness to make himself square without.

sentences.zh: 敬義立而德不孤，直方大則不疑其所行也。」

translations.literal: When reverence and righteousness are established, virtue is not alone; being straight, square, and great, he does not doubt the course he takes."
translations.idiomatic: When reverence and righteousness are established, virtue is not isolated; being straight, square, and great, he does not doubt what he does."

sentences.zh: 嵇康撰《釋私論》，曹羲著《至公篇》，皆以崇公激俗，抑私事主，一言可以蔽之，歸於體正而已矣。

translations.literal: Ji Kang wrote "On Explaining Selfishness" and Cao Xi authored "On Utmost Public-Mindedness"; both sought to exalt the public to rouse custom and restrain selfishness in serving the ruler—in a word, it all comes down to embodying uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Kang wrote "On Explaining Selfishness" and Cao Xi wrote "On Utmost Public-Mindedness"; both sought to exalt the public good, stir society, and restrain private interest in serving the ruler—in one phrase, it all comes down to embodying uprightness.

sentences.zh: 《禮記》曰：「刑者侀也，侀者成也，一成而不可變，故君子盡心焉。」

translations.literal: The Book of Rites says: "Punishment is the pattern; the pattern is completion; once completed it cannot be altered—therefore the noble person devotes his full heart to it."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Rites says: "Punishment is the pattern; the pattern is fulfillment; once fulfilled it cannot be changed—therefore the noble person gives it his whole heart."

sentences.zh: 若以喜怒制刑，輕重設比，是則橋前驚馬，用希旨論人，苑中獵兔，以從欲廢法。

translations.literal: If punishment is governed by joy and anger and light and heavy are set by comparison, then it is like startling a horse before the bridge—using sycophantic judgment of people—or hunting rabbits in the park, to abandon the law to follow one's desires.
translations.idiomatic: If punishment is controlled by mood and severity is decided by whim, that is like judging a case from a startled horse at the bridge—using flattery to decide a person's fate—or like hunting rabbits in the park and abandoning the law to satisfy desire.

sentences.zh: 理有違而合道，物貴和而不同，不同之和，正在其中矣。

translations.literal: Principle may seem to oppose yet still accord with the Way; things are prized for harmony yet not sameness—the harmony of not-sameness lies precisely within this.
translations.idiomatic: Principle may appear to conflict yet still accord with the Way; what matters is harmony, not sameness—and the harmony that preserves difference lies right here.

sentences.zh: 昔任延爲武威太守，漢帝誡之曰：「善事上官，無失名譽。」

translations.literal: In former times Ren Yan served as Administrator of Wuwei; the Han emperor admonished him, saying: "Serve your superiors well, and do not lose your reputation."
translations.idiomatic: In the past Ren Yan served as Administrator of Wuwei, and the Han emperor warned him: "Serve your superiors well and do not lose your good name."

sentences.zh: 延對曰：「臣聞忠臣不私，私臣不忠，上下雷同，非國家之福。

translations.literal: Yan replied: "I have heard that a loyal minister is not self-serving, and a self-serving minister is not loyal; when superiors and inferiors echo one another alike, it is not a blessing to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yan answered: "I have heard that a loyal minister is not self-serving, and a self-serving minister is not loyal; when superiors and subordinates merely echo one another, that is no blessing to the state.

sentences.zh: 善事上官，臣不敢奉詔。」

translations.literal: To serve superiors well—I dare not accept this edict."
translations.idiomatic: As for serving superiors well—I dare not obey that command."

sentences.zh: 任延雅奏，漢主是其言。

translations.literal: Ren Yan's elegant reply—the Han sovereign approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yan's fine reply pleased the Han emperor, who approved what he said.

sentences.zh: 此則歸正不回，乖旨順義，不以忤懷見忌，斯亦違而合道。

translations.literal: This is returning to uprightness without wavering, departing from the imperial intent yet following righteousness—not incurring resentment for offending the heart—this too is opposing yet accord with the Way.
translations.idiomatic: This is holding to uprightness without turning aside, departing from the emperor's words yet following righteousness—not being resented for giving offense—and this too is seeming to oppose yet still accord with the Way.

sentences.zh: 《晏子春秋》：景公見梁丘據曰：「據與我和。」

translations.literal: In the Spring and Autumn of Master Yan: Duke Jing saw Liangqiu Ju and said: "Ju is in harmony with me."
translations.idiomatic: In Master Yan's Spring and Autumn Annals, Duke Jing saw Liangqiu Ju and said: "Ju is in harmony with me."

sentences.zh: 晏子曰：「此同也。

translations.literal: Yanzi said: "This is sameness.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzi said: "That is sameness.

sentences.zh: 和者，君甘則臣酸，君淡則臣咸。

translations.literal: Harmony: when the lord finds it sweet, the minister finds it sour; when the lord finds it bland, the minister finds it salty.
translations.idiomatic: Harmony means that when the ruler finds something sweet, the minister finds it sour; when the ruler finds it bland, the minister finds it salty.

sentences.zh: 今據也，君甘亦甘，所謂同也，安得爲和？」

translations.literal: Now Ju—when the lord finds it sweet, he also finds it sweet; this is what is called sameness—how can it be called harmony?"
translations.idiomatic: But Ju, when the ruler finds something sweet, also finds it sweet—that is what is called sameness; how can it be called harmony?"

sentences.zh: 是以濟鹽梅以調羹，乃適平心之味；

translations.literal: Therefore by adding salt and plum to season the stew, one attains the flavor of an even heart;
translations.idiomatic: Thus by adding salt and sour plum to balance a stew, one achieves the taste of an even mind;

sentences.zh: 獻可否而論道，方恢政體之節。

translations.literal: offering approval or disapproval to discuss the Way is how to restore the measure of governance.
translations.idiomatic: offering assent or dissent in discussing the Way is how to restore the proper limits of government.

sentences.zh: 俟引正而遵度，故曰物貴和而不同。

translations.literal: Await being led by uprightness and observing the standards—hence it is said that things are prized for harmony yet not sameness.
translations.idiomatic: Wait to be guided by uprightness and follow the proper measure—hence it is said that what is valued is harmony, not sameness.

sentences.zh: 劉曼山辯和同之義，有旨哉！

translations.literal: Liu Manshan's exposition of the meaning of harmony and sameness—how pointed!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Manshan's discussion of the meaning of harmony and sameness—how apt!

sentences.zh: 若以不同見譏，未敢聞誨。

translations.literal: If you take disapproval for being different, I dare not hear your instruction.
translations.idiomatic: If you mean to reprove me for being different, I cannot accept that teaching.

sentences.zh: 客曰：和同乖訓，則已聞之。

translations.literal: The guest said: "As for harmony and sameness departing from instruction—I have already heard that.
translations.idiomatic: The guest said: "As for the teaching that harmony is not sameness—I have already heard it.

sentences.zh: 援法成而不變者，豈恤獄之寬憲耶？

translations.literal: But citing law as fixed and unchanging—does that show concern for leniency in adjudicating cases?"
translations.idiomatic: But if you invoke law as fixed and unchanging, does that show any concern for leniency in judging cases?"

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：「禦眾以寬。」

translations.literal: The Book of Documents says: "Govern the multitude with leniency."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says: "Lead the people with leniency."

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「寬則得眾。」

translations.literal: The Commentary says: "With leniency one gains the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: The Commentary says: "With leniency one wins the people.

sentences.zh: 若以嚴統物，異乎寬政矣。

translations.literal: If one governs things with strictness, that differs from lenient governance."
translations.idiomatic: If one governs people with severity, that is not lenient rule."

sentences.zh: 對曰：刑賞二柄，唯人主操之，崇厚任寬，是謂帝王之德。

translations.literal: He replied: "Punishment and reward are the two handles, wielded only by the sovereign; to honor magnanimity and employ leniency—this is called the virtue of an emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "Punishment and reward are the two handles, and only the ruler may wield them; to value generosity and apply leniency—this is the virtue of an emperor.

sentences.zh: 慎子曰：「以力役法者，百姓也；

translations.literal: Master Shen said: "Those who are subordinate to the law by force are the common people;
translations.idiomatic: Master Shen said: "Those who are compelled by force to obey the law are the common people;

sentences.zh: 以死守法者，有司也；

translations.literal: those who uphold the law even unto death are the officials;
translations.idiomatic: those who uphold the law even at the cost of their lives are the officials;

sentences.zh: 以道變法者，君上也。」

translations.literal: those who alter the law according to the Way are the ruler above."
translations.idiomatic: those who change the law according to the Way are the ruler above."

sentences.zh: 然則匪人臣所操。

translations.literal: Therefore these are not for ministers to wield.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore these are not handles for ministers to hold.

sentences.zh: 後魏遊肇之爲廷尉也，魏帝嘗私敕肇有所降恕，肇執而不從曰：「陛下自能恕之，豈足令臣曲筆也？」

translations.literal: In Later Wei, when You Zhao served as Minister of Justice, the Wei emperor once privately instructed Zhao to reduce or pardon someone; Zhao held firm and would not obey, saying: "Your Majesty can pardon on your own authority—how could that justify having me bend the record?"
translations.idiomatic: In Later Wei, when You Zhao was Minister of Justice, the Wei emperor once privately ordered him to reduce or pardon a sentence; Zhao refused and said: "Your Majesty may pardon as you wish—how could that justify asking me to distort the record?"

sentences.zh: 是知寬恕是君道，曲從非臣節。

translations.literal: From this we know that leniency and pardon belong to the way of the ruler, while bending compliance is not the integrity of a minister.
translations.idiomatic: From this we know that leniency belongs to the ruler's way, while bending the law is not a minister's proper duty.

sentences.zh: 人或未達斯旨，不料其務，以平刑爲峻，將曲法爲寬，謹守憲章，號爲深密。

translations.literal: Some people may not have penetrated this intent, and misapprehend the task—taking impartial punishment for harshness and twisted law for leniency; strictly keeping to the statutes and ordinances is denounced as deep and severe.
translations.idiomatic: Some people fail to grasp this point and misunderstand the task: they call impartial punishment harshness and bending the law leniency, and denounce strict adherence to the statutes as being rigid and severe.

sentences.zh: 《內律》：「釋種虧戒，一誅五百人，如來不救其罪。」

translations.literal: The Inner Vinaya says: "When the Shakya clan violated the precepts and five hundred men were executed at once, the Tathagata did not rescue them from their guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The Inner Vinaya says: "When the Shakya clan broke the precepts and five hundred men were put to death at once, the Tathagata did not save them from punishment.

sentences.zh: 豈謂佛法爲殘刻耶？

translations.literal: Could one say that Buddhist law is cruel and harsh?"
translations.idiomatic: Can one say that Buddhist teaching is cruel and severe?"

sentences.zh: 老子《道德經》云：「天網恢恢，疏而不漏。」

translations.literal: Laozi's Daodejing says: "Heaven's net is vast and wide; though sparse, nothing slips through.
translations.idiomatic: Laozi's Daodejing says: "Heaven's net is vast; though its mesh is wide, nothing escapes.

sentences.zh: 豈謂道教爲凝峻耶？

translations.literal: Could one say that the Way of the Dao is rigid and severe?"
translations.idiomatic: Can one say that the Way of the Dao is austere and harsh?"

sentences.zh: 《家語》曰：「王者之誅有五，而寢盜不預焉。」

translations.literal: The Family Conversations says: "The punishments of a king number five, and feigned theft is not among them.
translations.idiomatic: The Family Conversations says: "A king has five punishments, and false accusations of theft are not among them.

sentences.zh: 即心辯言偽之流。

translations.literal: That is, the sort who argue with hidden intent and speak falsely.
translations.idiomatic: That refers to those who argue with hidden motives and speak falsely.

sentences.zh: 《禮記》亦陳四殺，破律亂名之謂。

translations.literal: The Book of Rites also sets forth the four capital offenses—what is called violating statutes and disordering names.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Rites also lists four capital crimes—what is called breaking the law and corrupting proper names.

sentences.zh: 豈是儒家執禁，孔子之深文哉？

translations.literal: Could this mean that the Confucian school rigidly enforces prohibitions and that Confucius applied the letter of the law harshly?
translations.idiomatic: Can one say that Confucian teaching is rigid prohibition, or that Confucius applied the law with excessive severity?

sentences.zh: 此三教之用法者，所以明真諦，重玄猷，存天綱，立人極也。

translations.literal: The way these Three Teachings employ punishment is to clarify true principle, honor the profound design, preserve heaven's guiding cord, and establish man's supreme standard.
translations.idiomatic: The way these Three Teachings use punishment is to clarify true principle, honor the deepest design, preserve heaven's guiding net, and establish humanity's highest standard.

sentences.zh: 然則乾象震曜，天道明威。

translations.literal: Thus the Qian trigram shows the thunderbolt's gleam—Heaven's Way makes its awe manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the image of Qian is the flash of thunder—Heaven's Way makes its authority clear.

sentences.zh: 齊眾惟刑，百王所以垂範；

translations.literal: To bring the multitude into order, nothing but punishment—the hundred kings therefore transmit this model;
translations.idiomatic: To bring the people into order, nothing but punishment—this is the model handed down by the hundred kings;

sentences.zh: 析人以法，三後於是成功。

translations.literal: To distinguish men by law—the three sovereigns thereby succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: to distinguish people through law—the Three Sovereigns succeeded by this means.

sentences.zh: 所務掌憲決平，斯廷尉之職耳。

translations.literal: What is to be undertaken is holding the statutes, judging, and deciding impartially—this alone is the duty of the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: What must be done is to uphold the law, judge cases, and decide them fairly—this and nothing else is the duty of the Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「家人嗃嗃，無咎；

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: "The Family: stern admonitions, no blame;
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: "In the Family, stern admonitions—no blame;

sentences.zh: 婦子嘻嘻，終吝。」

translations.literal: wife and son merry and laughing—in the end, regret."
translations.idiomatic: when wife and children laugh and jest, in the end there comes remorse."

sentences.zh: 嚴於其家，可移於國。

translations.literal: Strictness in one's household may be transferred to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Strictness within one's household can be extended to govern the realm.

sentences.zh: 昔崔實達於理而作《政論》，仲長統曰：「凡爲人主，宜寫《政論》一通，置諸坐側。」

translations.literal: In former times Cui Shi, accomplished in reasoning, wrote the Political Treatise; Zhongchang Tong said: "Every person who is a lord ought to copy out one complete text of the Political Treatise and place it beside his seat."
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Cui Shi, skilled in principled government, wrote the Political Treatise. Zhongchang Tong said: "Every ruler ought to make one full copy of the Political Treatise and keep it beside his seat."

sentences.zh: 其大抵雲爲國者以嚴致平，非以寬致平者也。

translations.literal: Its general purport says that those who govern a state achieve order through severity, not through leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Its general thesis is that governing a state achieves order through strictness, not through indulgence.

sentences.zh: 然則稱嚴者不必逾條越制，凝網重罰，在於施隱括以矯枉，用平典以禁非。

translations.literal: Thus what is called severity need not exceed articles and transgress regulations, tighten the net and impose heavy punishments; it lies in applying hidden restraints to correct deviation, and using even statutes to forbid wrongdoing.
translations.idiomatic: What is called severity need not mean exceeding the code or layering on crushing punishments; it means applying firm discipline to correct excess, and using equitable statutes to forbid wrong.

sentences.zh: 刑故有常，罰輕無舍，人不易犯，防之難越故也。

translations.literal: Punishments therefore have fixed standards, light penalties are not set aside, people do not lightly offend—for because it is guarded, it is hard to transgress.
translations.idiomatic: Because punishments are fixed and even lighter penalties are never waived, people do not offend easily; guards are in place, and transgression is hard.

sentences.zh: 但人慢吏濁，偽積贓深，而曰以寬理之，可以無過。

translations.literal: Yet when people are lax, officials corrupt, falsehoods pile up and guilt runs deep, yet one says to govern them with leniency and that there can be no fault.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when the people are insolent, officials corrupt, and fraud and guilt have piled deep, to say that governing with leniency will leave no fault—

sentences.zh: 何異乎命王良禦駻，舍銜策於奔踶；

translations.literal: how is it different from commanding Wang Liang to drive a horse, and casting aside bit and whip amid rearing and kicking;
translations.idiomatic: how is that different from asking Wang Liang to drive a horse while throwing away bit and whip as it rears and kicks;

sentences.zh: 請俞跗攻疾，停藥石於膚腠！

translations.literal: or requesting Yu Fu to treat illness, and halting medicine and stone at the skin and flesh!
translations.idiomatic: or calling on the physician Yu Fu to treat a disease while withholding medicine at the very surface of the skin!

sentences.zh: 適見秋駕轉逸，膏肓更深，醫人僕夫，何功之有？

translations.literal: One would merely see the autumn carriage turn ever more reckless, the fatal illness grow deeper—what achievement would the physician and groom have?
translations.idiomatic: One would only watch the autumn carriage run ever wilder and the fatal disease sink deeper—what credit could physician or groom claim?

sentences.zh: 又謂僕曰：成法而變，唯帝王之命歟？

translations.literal: Again he said to the servant: To change established law—is that only by the sovereign's command?
translations.idiomatic: He asked me again: Can established law be altered only at an emperor's command?

sentences.zh: 對曰：何爲其然也？

translations.literal: The reply was: Why should it be so?
translations.idiomatic: I answered: Why should that be so?

sentences.zh: 昔漢武帝甥昭平君殺人，以公主子，廷尉上請論。

translations.literal: In former times Emperor Wu of Han's nephew Zhao Pingjun killed a man; as the son of a princess, the Minister of Justice submitted a memorial requesting judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Emperor Wu of Han's nephew Zhao Pingjun killed a man. Because he was a princess's son, the Minister of Justice submitted a petition for sentencing.

sentences.zh: 左右爲言，武帝垂涕嘆曰：「法令者，先帝之所造也，用親故誣先帝子法，吾何面目入高廟乎？

translations.literal: Those at his side spoke on his behalf; Emperor Wu shed tears and sighed, saying: "The statutes and ordinances are what the Former Emperor created; to use kinship to circumvent the Former Emperor's son's law—what face could I have to enter the High Temple?
translations.idiomatic: Those around him pleaded his case. Emperor Wu wept and sighed: "These laws were made by the Former Emperor; to use kinship to circumvent the law he laid down for his own son—how could I face entering the High Temple?

sentences.zh: 又下負萬人！」

translations.literal: Moreover I would fail the myriad people below!"
translations.idiomatic: And I would betray the myriad people below!"

sentences.zh: 乃可其奏。

translations.literal: He then approved the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Then he approved the petition.

sentences.zh: 近代隋文帝子秦王俊爲并州總管，以奢縱免官。

translations.literal: In recent times Emperor Wen of Sui's son Qin Wang Jun was Regional Commander of Bingzhou; for extravagance and license he was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times Emperor Wen of Sui's son, Prince of Qin Jun, served as regional commander of Bingzhou and was dismissed for extravagance and debauchery.

sentences.zh: 僕射楊素奏言：「王，陛下愛子，請舍其過。」

translations.literal: Vice Director Yang Su memorialized, saying: "The Prince is Your Majesty's beloved son; I beg that his offense be forgiven."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Yang Su memorialized: "Your Majesty's beloved son the prince—I beg that his offense be pardoned."

sentences.zh: 文帝曰：「法不可違。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen said: "The law cannot be violated.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen replied: "The law cannot be broken.

sentences.zh: 若如公意，我是五兒之父，非兆人之父，何不別制天子兒律乎？

translations.literal: If I followed your view, I would be father to my five sons alone, not father to the myriad people—why not separately enact statutes for the Son of Heaven's sons?
translations.idiomatic: If I did as you suggest, I would be father to my five sons only, not to the myriad people—why not draft a separate code for the emperor's sons?

sentences.zh: 我安能虧法！」

translations.literal: How could I impair the law!"
translations.idiomatic: How could I compromise the law!"

sentences.zh: 卒不許。

translations.literal: In the end he did not grant permission.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he refused.

sentences.zh: 此是帝王操法，協於禮經不變之義。

translations.literal: This is how sovereigns wield the law, in accord with the Book of Rites' meaning of unchanging principle.
translations.idiomatic: This is how emperors uphold the law—in line with the Rites' doctrine that what is right does not change.

sentences.zh: 況於秋官典職，司寇肅事，而可變動者乎！

translations.literal: How much less the Autumn Office's canonical duties and the Minister of Punishments' solemn affairs—could these be subject to alteration!
translations.idiomatic: How much less should the canonical duties of the Minister of Justice and the solemn business of criminal law be altered!

sentences.zh: 我皇睿哲登圖，高視巖廊之上；

translations.literal: Our Emperor, wise and enlightened, ascended the throne and looks down from above the cliff gallery;
translations.idiomatic: Our sage emperor has ascended the throne and gazes from the heights of the imperial hall;

sentences.zh: 宰衡明允就列，輯穆廟堂之下。

translations.literal: Chancellor and ministers, bright and fair, take their places; harmony reigns below the ancestral hall.
translations.idiomatic: chancellors and ministers, bright and impartial, stand in their ranks; harmony fills the court below.

sentences.zh: 乾坤交泰，日月光華，庶績其凝，眾工咸理。

translations.literal: Heaven and earth interpenetrate in peace; sun and moon shine forth; all achievements are solidified; every office is well ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth are in harmony; sun and moon shine bright; every task finds its fulfillment; every office is well governed.

sentences.zh: 聚以正也，僕幸利見大人；

translations.literal: Gathering through righteousness—this servant is fortunate to meet the great man;
translations.idiomatic: As the Changes says, 'Gathering through righteousness'—I am fortunate to serve one worthy of the name;

sentences.zh: 引其吉焉，期養正於下位。

translations.literal: I draw on its auspiciousness and look to cultivate righteousness from a lower station.
translations.idiomatic: I take its blessing and hope to cultivate integrity from my humble post.

sentences.zh: 中正是托，予何懼乎？

translations.literal: With centrality and correctness as my reliance, what have I to fear?
translations.idiomatic: With fairness and rectitude as my guide, what have I to fear?

sentences.zh: 夫君子百行之基，出處二途而已。

translations.literal: The foundation of the hundred conduct of the gentleman rests on only two paths: serving and withdrawing.
translations.idiomatic: The foundation of all a gentleman's conduct lies in only two paths: public service and withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 出則策名委質，行直道以事人，進善納忠，仰太階而緝政。

translations.literal: In serving he registers his name and commits his body, follows the straight path in serving others, advances goodness and offers loyalty, and looks up to the Grand Steps to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: In service he registers his name and pledges his loyalty, follows the straight path in serving others, advances good counsel and offers faithful remonstrance, and beneath the imperial steps helps govern the realm.

sentences.zh: 諤諤其節，思爲社稷之臣；

translations.literal: Upright and forthright in his integrity, he thinks to be a minister of the altars of soil and grain;
translations.idiomatic: Bold and uncompromising in principle, he aspires to be a true servant of the state;

sentences.zh: 謇謇匪躬，願參柱石之任。

translations.literal: steadfast and devoted without sparing himself, he wishes to share the burden of the pillar and stone.
translations.idiomatic: steadfast and selfless, he yearns to bear the weight of the realm like a pillar.

sentences.zh: 處則高謝公卿，孝友揚名，是亦爲政。

translations.literal: In withdrawal he loftily declines lord and minister; filial piety and friendship win renown—this too is governing.
translations.idiomatic: In retirement he politely declines high office; through filial piety and friendship he wins renown—and that too is a form of governance.

sentences.zh: 煙霞尚誌，其用永貞，行藏事業，心跡斯在。

translations.literal: The mist and rosy clouds are still his aspiration; his employment is forever steadfast; in action and withdrawal, in enterprise—the heart's trace lies here.
translations.idiomatic: Though he prefers the mists and peaks, his purpose remains constant; whether in action or retirement, the work of the heart is found in both.

sentences.zh: 至如水中泛泛，天下悠悠，執馭爲榮，掃門自媚，拜塵邀勢，括囊守祿，從來長息，以爲深恥。

translations.literal: As for drifting upon the water, the world vast and endless—holding the reins for glory, sweeping the gate to flatter oneself, bowing in the dust to court power, tying the purse to hold salary—from long ago he has kept silent, taking this as deep shame.
translations.idiomatic: But to drift like foam on water through this endless world—to drive another's chariot for glory, sweep gates to curry favor, bow in the dust for power, or clutch one's purse to hoard a salary—he has always held his tongue at such conduct and counted it deep shame.

sentences.zh: 客乃逡巡不對，遂無以間僕也。

translations.literal: The guest then hesitated and did not reply, and thus had no means to interrupt the servant.
translations.idiomatic: The visitor faltered and fell silent, with no further question to put to me.

sentences.zh: 中宗覽而嘉之。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhongzong read it and praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhongzong read the treatise and commended it.

sentences.zh: 稍遷駕部郎中。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Director in the Department of Chariots.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Director in the Bureau of Chariots.

sentences.zh: 景雲元年，累轉左御史中丞，尋遷大理少卿。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingyun, after successive transfers he became Left Censor-in-Chief, then shortly was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In 710, after several promotions he became Left Censor-in-Chief, and soon afterward was made Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 二年，制依漢置刺史監郡，於天下沖要大州置都督二十人，妙選有威重者爲之，遂拜志愔齊州都督，事竟不行。

translations.literal: In the second year, an edict followed Han in establishing Regional Inspectors to oversee commanderies; twenty Regional Commanders were appointed in crucial and important prefectures throughout the realm, men of outstanding authority carefully selected; Zhìyìn was then appointed Regional Commander of Qi Prefecture, but the matter in the end was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, an edict revived the Han practice of inspectors overseeing commanderies; twenty regional commanders were to be posted at key prefectures across the empire, chosen from men of outstanding standing. Wang Zhiyin was appointed regional commander of Qi Prefecture, but the plan was never implemented.

sentences.zh: 又授齊州刺史，充河南道按察使。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Governor of Qi Prefecture and served as Investigative Commissioner of Henan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed governor of Qi Prefecture and investigative commissioner for Henan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷汴州刺史，仍舊充河南道按察使。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Governor of Bian Prefecture, still serving as Investigative Commissioner of Henan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was transferred to governor of Bian Prefecture while continuing as investigative commissioner for Henan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 太極元年，又令以本官兼御史中丞、內供奉，特賜實封一百戸。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiji, he was again ordered to hold his current office concurrently as Censor-in-Chief and Internal Attendant, and was specially granted a substantive fief of one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In 712 he was ordered to retain his post while also serving as Censor-in-Chief and palace attendant, and was granted a substantive fief of one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋加銀青光祿大夫，拜戸部侍郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was given the additional title of Grand Master with Silver-Green Tally and appointed Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was given the additional title of Grand Master with Silver-Green Tally and appointed Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 出爲魏州刺史，轉揚州大都督府長史，俱充本道按察使。

translations.literal: He went out as Governor of Wei Prefecture, then transferred to Senior Administrator of Yangzhou Superior Prefecture; in both cases he served as Investigative Commissioner of the respective circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He left the capital to serve as governor of Wei Prefecture, then became senior administrator of Yangzhou Superior Prefecture, in each case serving as investigative commissioner for his circuit.

sentences.zh: 所在令行禁止，奸猾屏跡，境內肅然。

translations.literal: Wherever he was, orders were enforced and prohibitions observed; the cunning and wicked vanished from sight; within the borders all was orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served, his orders were obeyed; fraudsters disappeared; and his jurisdiction grew calm and orderly.

sentences.zh: 久之，召拜刑部尚書。

translations.literal: After a long time he was summoned and appointed Minister of the Ministry of Punishment.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was recalled and appointed Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 開元九年，上幸東都，令充京師留守。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kaiyuan, when the Emperor visited the Eastern Capital, he was ordered to serve as Commandant remaining in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In 721 the emperor traveled to the Eastern Capital and appointed him to remain behind as commandant of the capital.

sentences.zh: 十年，有京兆人權梁山偽稱襄王男，自號光帝，與其黨及左右屯營押官謀反。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, a man of Jingzhao named Quan Liangshan falsely claimed to be the son of the Prince of Xiang, styled himself Emperor Guang, and with his partisans and the Left Garrison Camp supervising officer plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In 722 a Jingzhao man named Quan Liangshan falsely claimed to be a son of the Prince of Xiang, styled himself Emperor Guang, and with his followers and an officer of the Left Garrison Camp plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 夜半時擁左屯營兵百餘人自景風、長樂等門斬關入宮城，將殺志愔，志愔逾墻避賊。

translations.literal: At midnight he led more than a hundred Left Garrison soldiers through the Jingfeng, Changle, and other gates, cutting the barriers to enter the palace city; intending to kill Zhìyìn, Zhìyìn climbed over the wall to flee the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight he led more than a hundred Left Garrison soldiers through the Jingfeng and Changle gates, broke through the barriers, and entered the palace city. Intending to kill Wang Zhiyin, Zhiyin climbed over a wall to escape the rebels.

sentences.zh: 俄而屯營兵潰散，翻殺梁山等五人，傳首東都，志愔遂以駭卒。

translations.literal: Before long the garrison soldiers scattered in rout, instead killed Liangshan and five others, sent their heads to the Eastern Capital, and Zhìyìn thereupon died of fright.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the garrison troops broke and fled, turned on Liangshan and killed him along with four others, sent their heads to the Eastern Capital—and Wang Zhiyin died of shock.

sentences.zh: 盧從願盧從願，相州臨漳人，後魏度支尚書昶六代孫也。

translations.literal: Lu Congyuan—Lu Congyuan was a native of Linzhang in Xiang Prefecture, sixth-generation descendant of Chang, Minister of Revenue of Northern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Congyuan was a native of Linzhang in Xiang Prefecture, a sixth-generation descendant of Lu Chang, Minister of Revenue of Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 自范陽徙家焉，世爲山東著姓。

translations.literal: His family had moved from Fanyang and settled there, for generations a prominent surname of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: His clan had moved from Fanyang and settled there, becoming over generations one of the great families of the east.

sentences.zh: 冠明經舉，授絳州夏縣尉，又應制舉，拜右拾遺。

translations.literal: At the capping age he passed the Mingjing examination and was appointed District Magistrate of Xia County in Jiang Prefecture; he also answered the imperial special examination and was appointed Reminder of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: In early adulthood he passed the Classics examination and was appointed magistrate of Xia County in Jiang Prefecture; after also passing the imperial special examination he was made Right Reminder.

sentences.zh: 俄遷右肅政監察御史，充山南道黜陟巡撫使，奉使稱旨，拜殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Supervising Censor of the Right Bureau of Surveillance; as Commissioner of Promotion and Demotion and Tour of Inspection of Shannan Circuit he fulfilled the mission to the Emperor's satisfaction and was appointed Palace Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he became supervising censor of the Right Surveillance Bureau and served as touring commissioner for Shannan Circuit; his mission pleased the throne, and he was appointed palace censor.

sentences.zh: 累遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: After successive promotions he became Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to drafting secretary of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 睿宗踐祚，拜吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, he was appointed Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong came to the throne, he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 中宗之後，選司頗失綱紀，從願精心條理，大稱平允。

translations.literal: After Emperor Zhongzong, the Selection Office had largely lost its standards; Congyuan carefully set them in order and was greatly praised for fairness.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Zhongzong's reign the Selection Office had largely lost discipline; Congyuan reorganized it with great care and won wide praise for fairness.

sentences.zh: 其有冒名偽選及虛增功狀之類，皆能擿發其事。

translations.literal: Cases of assuming false names, fraudulent selection, and falsely inflated merit records and the like—he was able to expose them all.
translations.idiomatic: He could uncover every kind of fraud, from false names and bogus appointments to inflated merit records.

sentences.zh: 典選六年，前後無及之者。

translations.literal: He conducted selection for six years; before and after, none matched him.
translations.idiomatic: For six years he ran appointments, and no one before or since equaled him.

sentences.zh: 上嘉之，特與一子太子通事舍人。

translations.literal: The Emperor commended him and specially granted one of his sons the post of Palace Secretary of the Crown Prince's Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended him and specially granted one of his sons the post of secretary in the Crown Prince's service.

sentences.zh: 從願上疏乞回恩贈父，乃贈其父吉陽丞敬一爲鄭州長史。

translations.literal: Congyuan submitted a memorial requesting to turn the grace back to posthumously honor his father; his father Jingyi, Assistant Magistrate of Jiyang, was then posthumously appointed Senior Administrator of Zheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Congyuan memorialized asking to redirect the favor to his father; his father Jingyi, former assistant magistrate of Jiyang, was posthumously given the title of senior administrator of Zheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，高宗時裴行儉、馬載爲吏部，最爲稱職。

translations.literal: Formerly, during Emperor Gaozong's reign, Pei Xingjian and Ma Zai served in the Ministry of Personnel and were regarded as most competent.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Gaozong, Pei Xingjian and Ma Zai had been the most admired ministers of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 及是，從願與李朝隱同時典選，亦有美譽。

translations.literal: At this time Congyuan and Li Chaoyin concurrently conducted selection, and likewise enjoyed a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Now Congyuan and Li Chaoyin ran appointments together and likewise won high praise.

sentences.zh: 時人稱曰：吏部前有馬、裴，後有盧、李。

translations.literal: People of the time said: Before in the Ministry of Personnel there were Ma and Pei; afterward there are Lu and Li.
translations.idiomatic: People said: In Personnel, Ma and Pei came first; Lu and Li came after.

sentences.zh: 開元四年，上盡召新授縣令，一時於殿庭策試，考入下第者，一切放歸學問。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaiyuan, the Emperor summoned all newly appointed district magistrates and at one time tested them by written examination in the palace court; those who scored in the lower ranks were all released to return to study.
translations.idiomatic: In 716 the emperor summoned all newly appointed county magistrates and tested them at once in the palace hall; those who scored lowest were sent back to their studies.

sentences.zh: 從願以註擬非才，左遷豫州刺史。

translations.literal: Congyuan, because his proposed appointments were of unqualified men, was demoted to Governor of Yu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Because Congyuan had recommended unqualified candidates, he was demoted to governor of Yu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 爲政嚴簡，按察使奏課爲天下第一等，璽書勞問，賜絹百匹。

translations.literal: His governance was strict and concise; the investigative commissioner reported his evaluation as highest in the realm, and an imperial seal letter commended him and granted a hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with strict simplicity; the circuit commissioner rated his performance the best in the empire; the emperor sent a sealed letter of commendation and awarded him a hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 無幾，入爲工部侍郎，轉尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Before long he entered the capital as Vice Minister of the Ministry of Works, then transferred to Left Assistant in the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled as Vice Minister of Works, then promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 又與楊滔及吏部侍郎裴漼、禮部侍郎王丘、中書舍人劉令植刪定《開元後格》，遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He also joined Yang Tao, Vice Minister of Personnel Pei Hui, Vice Minister of Rites Wang Qiu, and Drafting Secretary Liu Lingzhi in revising the Statutes after Kaiyuan, and was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Yang Tao, Vice Minister Pei Hui, Vice Minister Wang Qiu, and drafting secretary Liu Lingzhi, he revised the post-Kaiyuan statutes and was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十一年，拜工部尚書，加銀青光祿大夫，仍令東都留守。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was appointed Minister of the Ministry of Works, given the additional title of Grand Master with Silver-Green Tally, and again ordered to remain as Commandant of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In 723 he was made Minister of Works, given the additional title of Grand Master with Silver-Green Tally, and again ordered to stay behind as commandant of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 十三年，從升泰山，又加金紫光祿大夫，代韋抗爲刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he followed the ascent of Mount Tai, was again given the title of Grand Master with Golden-Green Tally, and replaced Wei Kang as Minister of the Ministry of Punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In 725 he accompanied the emperor on the Mount Tai rites, was further promoted to Grand Master with Golden-Green Tally, and replaced Wei Kang as Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 頻年充校京外官考使，前後咸稱允當。

translations.literal: For several years in succession he served as Evaluator of Outer Officials outside the capital, and before and after all called his work fair and appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: For several years he served as commissioner evaluating officials outside the capital, and each time was praised for his fair judgments.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞宇文融承恩用事，以括獲田戸之功，本司校考爲上下，從願抑不與之。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Yuwen Rong, relying on imperial favor, wielded power; for his achievement in registering land and households, his department's evaluation was graded upper-middle, but Congyuan suppressed it and would not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Yuwen Rong traded on imperial favor for power; for his work registering land and households his office deserved an upper-middle rating, but Congyuan refused to grant it.

sentences.zh: 融頗以爲恨，密奏從願廣占良田，至有百餘頃。

translations.literal: Rong was quite resentful and secretly memorialized that Congyuan had seized broad tracts of good farmland, reaching more than a hundred qing.
translations.idiomatic: Rong bore a deep grudge and secretly reported that Congyuan had seized vast tracts of good farmland—more than a hundred qing.

sentences.zh: 其後，上嘗擇堪爲宰相者，或薦從願，上曰：「從願廣占田園，是不廉也。」

translations.literal: Afterward, when the Emperor once chose someone capable of being Chancellor, someone recommended Congyuan; the Emperor said: "Congyuan has seized vast estates and gardens—this is not incorrupt."
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the emperor sought someone fit for chancellor, Congyuan was recommended; the emperor said: "Congyuan has hoarded vast estates—that shows a lack of integrity."

sentences.zh: 遂止不用。

translations.literal: He thereupon stopped and did not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: And so the appointment went no further.

sentences.zh: 從願又因早朝，途中爲人所射，中其從者，捕賊竟不獲。

translations.literal: Congyuan also, while going to early audience, was shot at on the road by someone; his attendant was hit; the thief was pursued but ultimately not captured.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion, while on his way to morning audience, someone fired at Congyuan on the road and struck his attendant; the assailant was never caught.

sentences.zh: 時議從願久在選司，爲被抑者所讎。

translations.literal: Public opinion held that Congyuan's long tenure in the Selection Office made him the target of revenge by those he had suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many believed that his long years in Personnel had made him enemies among those he had passed over.

sentences.zh: 十六年，東都留守。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, he was Eastern Capital Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In 728 he served as commandant of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 時坐子起居郎論糶米入官有剩利，爲憲司所糾，出爲絳州刺史，再遷太子賓客。

translations.literal: At that time because his son, the Attendant of the Left, was implicated for selling rice to the government with surplus profit, he was impeached by the Censorate, sent out as Governor of Jiang Prefecture, and after a second transfer became Guest of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: When his son, a palace attendant, was impeached for profiting from selling rice to the government, Congyuan was censured, demoted to governor of Jiang Prefecture, and later made advisor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 二十年，河北谷貴，敕從願爲宣撫處置使，開倉以救饑餒。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, grain was costly in Hebei; an edict appointed Congyuan Pacification and Disposition Commissioner; he opened the granaries to relieve hunger.
translations.idiomatic: In 732, when grain prices soared in Hebei, the emperor appointed Congyuan pacification commissioner; he opened the granaries to relieve famine.

sentences.zh: 使回，以年老抗表乞骸骨，乃拜吏部尚書，聽致仕，給全祿。

translations.literal: When the mission returned, because of old age he forcefully submitted a memorial requesting to retire on account of infirmity; he was then appointed Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, permitted to retire from office, and granted full salary.
translations.idiomatic: When his mission ended, citing old age he memorialized to retire; the emperor made him Minister of Personnel, granted him retirement, and continued his full salary.

sentences.zh: 二十五年卒，年七十餘，贈益州大都督，謚曰文。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he died, aged over seventy; posthumously invested as Governor-General of Yi Prefecture, posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 737 at over seventy; posthumously he was given the title of governor-general of Yi Prefecture and the posthumous name Wen.

sentences.zh: 李朝隱李朝隱，京兆三原人也。

translations.literal: Li Chaoyin—Li Chaoyin was a native of Sanyuan in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chaoyin was a native of Sanyuan in the Jingzhao region.

sentences.zh: 少以明法舉，拜臨汾尉，累授大理丞。

translations.literal: In youth he passed the examination in understanding law and was appointed Military Aide of Linfen; after successive appointments he became Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he passed the legal examination and was appointed aide in Linfen; he rose in succession to assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 神龍年，功臣敬暉、桓彥範爲武三思所構，諷侍御史鄭愔奏請誅之，敕大理結其罪。

translations.literal: In the Shenlong era, the meritorious ministers Jing Hui and Huan Yanfan were framed by Wu Sansi; he prompted Censor-in-Attendance Zheng Yin to memorialize requesting their execution; an edict ordered the Court of Judicial Review to fix their guilt.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenlong reign the meritorious ministers Jing Hui and Huan Yanfan were framed by Wu Sansi, who induced Attendant Censor Zheng Yin to memorialize for their execution; an edict ordered the Court of Judicial Review to convict them.

sentences.zh: 朝隱以暉等所犯，不經推窮，未可即正刑名。

translations.literal: Chaoyin held that the offenses of Hui and the others, without having undergone thorough investigation, could not immediately be fixed with penal names.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyin argued that Hui and the others had not been fully investigated and could not yet be formally sentenced.

sentences.zh: 時裴談爲大理卿，異筆斷斬，仍籍沒其家，朝隱由是忤旨。

translations.literal: At that time Pei Tan was Director of the Court of Judicial Review; with a different brush he sentenced them to decapitation and also confiscated their households; Chaoyin thereby violated the imperial intent.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Tan, then director of the court, wrote a different verdict ordering their execution and confiscation of their property—and Chaoyin thereby defied the throne.

sentences.zh: 中宗令貶嶺南惡處，侍中韋巨源、中書令李嶠奏曰：「朝隱素稱清正，斷獄亦甚當事，一朝遠徙嶺表，恐天下疑其罪。」

translations.literal: Emperor Zhongzong ordered him demoted to an evil place in Lingnan; Attendant-in-Chief Wei Juyuan and Grand Secretary Li Qiao memorialized, saying: "Chaoyin has long been known as pure and upright; in deciding cases he is also very much to the point; to banish him far to the region south of the mountains in one morning—I fear the realm will doubt the nature of his offense."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhongzong ordered him exiled to a harsh region of Lingnan. Chief Minister Wei Juyuan and Grand Secretary Li Qiao memorialized: "Chaoyin has long been known for integrity, and his judicial decisions are sound; to exile him overnight to the far south would make the empire doubt his guilt."

sentences.zh: 中宗意解，出爲聞喜令。

translations.literal: The Emperor's intent eased; he was sent out as Magistrate of Wenxi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relented and sent Chaoyin out as magistrate of Wenxi.

sentences.zh: 尋遷侍御史，三遷長安令，有宦官閭興貴詣縣請托，朝隱命拽出之。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Attendant Censor; after three promotions he became Magistrate of Chang'an; the eunuch Lü Xinggui came to the district with a request for favor, and Chaoyin ordered him dragged out.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became attendant censor and, after three promotions, magistrate of Chang'an. When the eunuch Lü Xinggui came to the county office seeking favors, Chaoyin ordered him thrown out.

sentences.zh: 睿宗聞而嘉嘆，廷召朝隱，勞曰：「卿爲京縣令能如此，朕復何憂。」

translations.literal: Emperor Ruizong heard and praised him with admiration; he summoned Chaoyin in audience and encouraged him, saying: "You as magistrate of the capital county can act thus—what have I to worry about?"
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong heard this he praised Chaoyin warmly, summoned him to court, and said: "If the magistrate of the capital county can act like this, what have I to worry about?"

sentences.zh: 乃下制曰：「夫不吐剛而謅上、不茹柔而黷下者，君子之事也。

translations.literal: Then an edict was issued, saying: "Not spitting out the hard to fawn on superiors, not swallowing the soft to corrupt inferiors—this is the affair of the gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Then an imperial edict declared: "A gentleman does not swallow hard truths to flatter his superiors, nor indulge the soft-spoken to corrupt those below.

sentences.zh: 踐霤必繩、登車無屈者，正人之務也。

translations.literal: Treading wet ground one must apply the line; mounting the carriage without bending—this is the duty of the upright man.
translations.idiomatic: To apply the rule even when treading wet ground, to stand straight even when mounting a carriage—such is the duty of an upright man.

sentences.zh: 長安縣令李朝隱，德義不回，清強自遂，亟聞嘉政，累著能名。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Chang'an Li Chaoyin—virtuous and righteous without turning aside, pure and strong in pursuing his course, repeatedly heard of for excellent governance, repeatedly distinguished for ability and fame.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chaoyin, magistrate of Chang'an, is upright and resolute, pure and firm in his ways; his excellent governance is widely praised, and his reputation for ability stands proven.

sentences.zh: 近者品官入縣，有乖儀式，遂能責之以禮，繩之以愆。

translations.literal: Recently when a ranked official entered the district and deviated from proper form, he was able to hold him to account with rites and bind him with fault.
translations.idiomatic: Recently when a ranked official entered the county office in improper fashion, Chaoyin held him to account by ritual propriety and punished his breach.

sentences.zh: 但閹豎之流，多有憑恃，柔寬之代，必弄威權。

translations.literal: Yet the sort of castrated attendants mostly have someone to rely upon; in an age of softness and leniency, they are sure to wield power and authority.
translations.idiomatic: Yet eunuchs often have powerful patrons; in an age of lenient rule they invariably abuse their authority.

sentences.zh: 歷觀載籍，常所嘆息。

translations.literal: Reviewing the records through the ages, one often sighs.
translations.idiomatic: A reading of the historical records shows how often one must sigh.

sentences.zh: 朕規誡前古，勤求典憲，能副朕意，實賴斯人。

translations.literal: I take warning from former ages and diligently seek the statutes and ordinances; that one could fulfill my intent truly relies on this man.
translations.idiomatic: I have taken warning from the past and diligently sought to uphold the code of laws; that my aims can be fulfilled truly depends on this man.

sentences.zh: 昔虞延持皇后之客，梅陶鞭太子之傅，古稱遺直，復見於今。

translations.literal: In former times Yu Yan detained the empress's guest; Mei Tao flogged the crown prince's tutor—antiquity called this upright legacy, and it is seen again today.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Yu Yan detained the empress's guest and Mei Tao flogged the crown prince's tutor; antiquity praised such unyielding integrity, and it appears again in our day.

sentences.zh: 思欲旌其美行，遷以重職，爲時屬閱戸，政在養人，宜加一階，用表剛烈。

translations.literal: I intend to commend his fine conduct and promote him to a weighty office; at this time the realm needs household inspection, governance lies in nourishing the people—it is fitting to add one rank to display his stern integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to honor his exemplary conduct with a weightier post—at a time when the realm needs household registration and governance rests on nurturing the people—I grant him one additional rank to mark his steadfast integrity.

sentences.zh: 可太中大夫。

translations.literal: He may be made Grand Master of Palace Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He is appointed Grand Master of Palace Attendance.

sentences.zh: 特賜中上考，兼絹百匹。」

translations.literal: He is specially granted an upper-middle performance rating, together with a hundred bolts of silk."
translations.idiomatic: He is specially awarded an upper-middle evaluation and a hundred bolts of silk."

sentences.zh: 七遷絳州刺史，兼知吏部選事。

translations.literal: After seven promotions he became Governor of Jiang Prefecture, concurrently overseeing the Ministry of Personnel's selection affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After several promotions he became governor of Jiang Prefecture and concurrently oversaw appointments in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 開元二年，遷吏部侍郎，銓敘平允，甚爲當時所稱，降璽書褒美，授一子太子通事舍人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyuan he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel; his rating and selection were fair and equitable, greatly praised at the time; an imperial seal letter was sent in commendation, and one of his sons was granted the post of Palace Secretary of the Crown Prince's Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 714 he was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel; his appointments were fair and widely praised; the emperor sent a sealed letter of commendation and granted one of his sons the post of secretary in the crown prince's service.

sentences.zh: 四年春，以授縣令非其人，出爲滑州刺史，轉同州刺史。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year, because the appointed district magistrates were unqualified, he was sent out as Governor of Hua Prefecture and transferred to Governor of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 716, because the county magistrates he had recommended proved unfit, he was demoted to governor of Hua Prefecture and then transferred to governor of Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 駕幸東都，路由同州，朝隱蒙旨召見賞慰，賜衣一副、絹百匹。

translations.literal: When the Emperor visited the Eastern Capital and passed through Tong Prefecture, Chaoyin was summoned by imperial order, received and comforted, and granted one set of robes and a hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor traveled to the Eastern Capital and passed through Tong Prefecture, Chaoyin was summoned to audience, praised and comforted, and awarded one set of robes and a hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 尋遷河南尹，政甚清嚴，豪右屏跡。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Intendant of Henan; his governance was very strict and stern, and the powerful families vanished from sight.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made intendant of Henan; he governed with stern integrity, and the local magnates disappeared from view.

sentences.zh: 時太子舅趙常奴恃勢侵害平人，朝隱曰：「此而不繩，何以爲政？」

translations.literal: At the time the crown prince's maternal uncle Zhao Changnu relied on his influence to harm common people. Chaoyin said: "If this is not bound by law, how can one govern?"
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince's maternal uncle Zhao Changnu used his influence to bully commoners, Chaoyin said: "If I do not punish this, how can I govern?"

sentences.zh: 執而杖之。

translations.literal: He seized and flogged him.
translations.idiomatic: He had him seized and beaten with the rod.

sentences.zh: 上聞，又降敕書慰勉之。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard, he again sent an edict letter to comfort and encourage him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it, he sent another edict to comfort and encourage him.

sentences.zh: 十年，遷大理卿。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was transferred to Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In 722 he was made director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 時武強令裴景仙犯乞取贓積五千匹，事發逃走。

translations.literal: At the time the magistrate of Wuqiang, Pei Jingxian, committed the crime of solicited bribery totaling five thousand bolts; when the affair came to light he fled.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Pei Jingxian, magistrate of Wuqiang, was found to have extorted bribes totaling five thousand bolts of silk; when the case broke, he fled.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，令集眾殺之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly angered and ordered him seized and publicly executed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered him seized and executed before the assembled crowd.

sentences.zh: 朝隱執奏曰：「裴景仙縁是乞贓，犯不至死。

translations.literal: Chaoyin firmly memorialized, saying: "Pei Jingxian's offense is solicited bribery, and the crime does not reach death.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyin submitted a firm memorial: "Pei Jingxian's offense is extortion through solicitation; it does not warrant death.

sentences.zh: 又景仙曾祖故司空寂，往屬締構，首預元勛。

translations.literal: Moreover Jingxian's great-grandfather, the late Grand Director Pei Ji, in former days assisted in founding the realm and was among the first meritorious ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Jingxian's great-grandfather, the late Grand Director Pei Ji, helped found the dynasty and was numbered among its foremost meritorious ministers.

sentences.zh: 載初年中，家陷非罪，凡有兄弟皆被誅夷，唯景仙獨存，今見承嫡。

translations.literal: In the Zaichu era his household fell into false guilt; all his brothers were executed, only Jingxian alone survived, and he now stands as the direct heir.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zaichu era his family was ruined on false charges; all his brothers were executed, and Jingxian alone survived as the direct heir.

sentences.zh: 據贓未當死坐，準犯猶入請條。

translations.literal: According to the amount of bribes, the offense does not merit death; by the standard for the offense he still falls under the commutation provisions.
translations.idiomatic: By the amount of bribes involved, the offense does not merit death; under the statute it still falls within the provisions for commuted punishment.

sentences.zh: 十代宥賢，功實宜録；

translations.literal: Ten generations' pardon for meritorious ancestors—merit truly should be recorded;
translations.idiomatic: The law grants ten generations' pardon for ancestral merit, and such service truly deserves recognition;

sentences.zh: 一門絶祀，情或可哀。

translations.literal: a whole clan's line extinguished—the circumstance may permit pity.
translations.idiomatic: yet an entire clan's line would be extinguished—a circumstance that may move one to pity.

sentences.zh: 願寬暴市之刑，俾就投荒之役，則舊勛斯允。」

translations.literal: I wish to lighten the punishment of public execution and permit exile to the wilderness instead; then the old merit would be fittingly honored."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the sentence of public execution be commuted to exile in the wilderness, so that the family's old merit may still be honored."

sentences.zh: 手詔不許。

translations.literal: An imperial letter in the Emperor's own hand did not grant permission.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied in his own hand and refused.

sentences.zh: 朝隱又奏曰：

translations.literal: Chaoyin again memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyin memorialized again:

sentences.zh: 有斷自天，處之極法。

translations.literal: When judgment is passed from on high, apply the extreme penalty.
translations.idiomatic: When Heaven itself passes judgment, the extreme penalty may be applied.

sentences.zh: 生殺之柄，人主合專；

translations.literal: The power of life and death appropriately belongs solely to the sovereign;
translations.idiomatic: The power of life and death rightly belongs to the sovereign alone;

sentences.zh: 輕生有條，臣下當守。

translations.literal: when sparing life there are statutes; ministers should uphold them.
translations.idiomatic: but when sparing life, there are statutes—and ministers must uphold them.

sentences.zh: 枉法者，枉理而取，十五匹便抵死刑；

translations.literal: For those who pervert the law—taking by perverted reasoning—fifteen bolts already warrant the death penalty;
translations.idiomatic: One who perverts the law and takes bribes by abuse of office faces death at fifteen bolts;

sentences.zh: 乞取者，因乞爲贓，數千匹止當流坐。

translations.literal: for extortion through solicitation—several thousand bolts only warrant exile.
translations.idiomatic: one who extorts bribes through solicitation, even for several thousand bolts, faces only exile.

sentences.zh: 今若乞取得罪，便處斬刑，後有枉法當科，欲加何辟？

translations.literal: If extortion through solicitation now receives decapitation, when later there is perverting the law to be punished, what penalty could be added?
translations.idiomatic: If extortion is punished with decapitation today, what penalty remains for the far graver crime of perverting the law tomorrow?

sentences.zh: 所以爲國惜法，期守律文，非敢以法隨人，曲矜仙命。

translations.literal: Therefore I cherish the law for the state's sake, hoping to uphold the statute text—not daring to bend the law to the person and warp favor for Jingxian's life.
translations.idiomatic: I speak thus to preserve the law for the state, not to bend the law to save Jingxian's life.

sentences.zh: 射兔魏苑，驚馬漢橋，初震皇赫，竟從廷議，豈威不能制，而法貴有常。

translations.literal: Shooting a hare in Wei's park, startling horses at Han's bridge—initially the sovereign's wrath was shaken, yet in the end the court's deliberation was followed; can might not control, yet the law values constancy.
translations.idiomatic: When an emperor shot a hare in the Wei park or when horses panicked at Han's bridge, imperial wrath flared at first—yet in the end the court's counsel prevailed. Is authority powerless to restrain? No—but the law must remain constant.

sentences.zh: 又景仙曾祖寂，草昧忠節，定爲元勛，位至臺司，恩倍常數。

translations.literal: Moreover Jingxian's great-grandfather Ji, in the chaos of founding showed loyal integrity and was fixed as a meritorious minister; he reached the highest office, and grace exceeded the ordinary measure.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Jingxian's great-grandfather Ji served with loyal integrity in the founding chaos and was counted among the dynasty's foremost meritorious ministers; he rose to the highest office and received grace beyond the ordinary measure.

sentences.zh: 載初之際，被枉破家，諸子各犯非辜，唯仙今見承嫡。

translations.literal: At the Zaichu juncture, wrongfully ruined and household destroyed, each son suffered innocent guilt; only Jingxian now survives as direct heir.
translations.idiomatic: At the Zaichu juncture the family was wrongfully destroyed; each son suffered innocent guilt, and only Jingxian survives as the direct heir.

sentences.zh: 若寂勛都棄，仙罪特加，則叔向之賢何足稱者，若敖之鬼不其餧而？

translations.literal: If Ji's merit is wholly discarded and Jingxian's guilt specially increased, then how does the worth of Shuxiang merit praise—would the ghost of Ru'ao not go hungry?
translations.idiomatic: If Ji's merit is cast aside and Jingxian's guilt is specially aggravated, of what worth is the virtue of Shuxiang—and will not the ghost of Ru'ao go hungry?

sentences.zh: 舍罪念功，乞垂天聽。

translations.literal: Setting aside guilt to consider merit—I beg you heed this in heaven's hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Set guilt aside and consider merit—I beg Your Majesty to hear this plea.

sentences.zh: 應敕決杖及有犯配流，近發德音，普標殊澤，杖者既聽減數，流者仍許給程。

translations.literal: Those subject to edict-mandated flogging and those sentenced to exile—recently a benevolent proclamation was issued, universally marking special grace; those to be flogged were permitted reduction in count, and those exiled were still permitted travel allowance.
translations.idiomatic: Those subject to flogging by imperial edict and those sentenced to exile have lately received a benevolent proclamation granting special grace: flogging may be reduced, and exiles may receive travel provisions.

sentences.zh: 天下颙颙，孰不幸甚！

translations.literal: All under heaven look up with eager hope—who would not consider it great fortune!
translations.idiomatic: All under heaven look up with eager hope—who would not count himself blessed!

sentences.zh: 瞻彼四海，已被深恩，豈於一人，獨峻常典？

translations.literal: Behold the four seas, already granted deep grace—how for one man alone apply harsh ordinary statutes?
translations.idiomatic: The four seas have already received Your Majesty's deep grace—why apply harsh ordinary statutes to this one man alone?

sentences.zh: 伏乞采臣之議，致仙於法。

translations.literal: I humbly beg you adopt my proposal and subject Jingxian to the law.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg Your Majesty to adopt my proposal and subject Jingxian to the law as written.

sentences.zh: 乃下制曰：「罪不在大，本乎情；

translations.literal: Then an edict was issued, saying: "Guilt does not lie in magnitude but in intent;
translations.idiomatic: Then an imperial edict declared: "Guilt lies not in magnitude but in intent;

sentences.zh: 罰在必行，不在重。

translations.literal: punishment lies in certain execution, not in severity.
translations.idiomatic: punishment lies in certainty of execution, not in severity.

sentences.zh: 朕垂範作訓，庶動植咸若，豈嚴刑逞戮，使手足無措者哉？

translations.literal: I set examples to instruct, hoping all living things accord—how could I indulge severe punishments and slaughter, leaving hands and feet nowhere to rest?
translations.idiomatic: I set examples to instruct all living things—how could I indulge in harsh punishments and slaughter, leaving my subjects with nowhere to turn?

sentences.zh: 裴景仙幸藉緒余，超升令宰，輕我憲法，蠹我風猷，不慎畏知之金，詎識無貪之寶，家盈黷貨，身乃逃亡。

translations.literal: Pei Jingxian fortunately relied on family pedigree, rose above to district magistrate, treated my laws lightly, corrupted my moral sway, did not carefully heed the gold of respectful knowledge, how could he know the treasure of non-greed—household overflowing with corrupt goods, and he himself fled.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Jingxian traded on family connections to rise to district magistrate, treated my laws lightly, and corrupted public morals. He did not heed the warning that power demands restraint, nor cherish the treasure of integrity; his household overflowed with ill-gotten goods, and he himself fled.

sentences.zh: 殊不知天孽可違，自愆難逭，所以不從本法，加以殊刑，冀懲貪暴之流，以塞侵漁之路。

translations.literal: Yet he did not know heaven's affliction may be defied but one's own fault hard to escape—therefore not following the ordinary law but adding extraordinary punishment, hoping to punish the greedy and violent stream and block the path of encroachment and predation.
translations.idiomatic: He did not understand that heaven's judgment may be defied but one's own guilt cannot be escaped. I therefore set aside the ordinary law and imposed an extraordinary penalty, hoping to deter the greedy and block the path of predatory corruption.

sentences.zh: 然以其祖父昔預經綸，佐命有功，締構斯重，緬懷賞延之義，俾協政寬之典，宜舍其極法，以竄遐荒。

translations.literal: Yet because his grandfather and father formerly participated in statecraft, assisted the mandate with merit, the founding enterprise being weighty—recalling the principle of extending rewards, to accord with the clemency of governance—he should be spared the extreme penalty and sent to the far wilderness.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because his grandfather and father once served in founding the state and earned merit in assisting the mandate, and mindful of the principle of extending rewards in governance, he should be spared the extreme penalty and exiled to the far wilderness.

sentences.zh: 仍決杖一百，流嶺南惡處。」

translations.literal: Still sentenced to a hundred blows with the rod and exile to a harsh place in Lingnan."
