translations.idiomatic: He was sentenced to a hundred blows with the rod and exile to a harsh region of Lingnan."

sentences.zh: 朝隱俄轉岐州刺史，母憂去官。

translations.literal: Chaoyin soon transferred to Governor of Qi Prefecture; upon his mother's death he left office.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyin was soon transferred to governor of Qi Prefecture; when his mother died he resigned to mourn.

sentences.zh: 起爲揚州大都督府長史，抗疏固辭，制許之。

translations.literal: Recalled as Senior Administrator of Yangzhou Superior Prefecture, he memorialized firmly declining; an edict granted permission.
translations.idiomatic: When recalled as senior administrator of Yangzhou Superior Prefecture, he submitted a firm memorial declining the appointment, and the emperor granted his request.

sentences.zh: 朝隱性孝友，時年已衰暮，在喪尤加毀瘠。

translations.literal: Chaoyin was by nature filial and friendly; by then already aged, in mourning he became especially emaciated.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyin was by nature filial and devoted; though already advanced in years, in mourning he wasted away still further.

sentences.zh: 明年，制又起爲揚州長史，不獲已而就職，復入爲大理卿，累封金城伯，代崔隱甫爲御史大夫。

translations.literal: The next year an edict again recalled him as Senior Administrator of Yangzhou; unable to refuse he took the post; again entered as Director of the Court of Judicial Review, cumulatively enfeoffed as Earl of Jincheng, and replaced Cui Yinfu as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The next year another edict recalled him as senior administrator of Yangzhou; unable to refuse, he took the post. He returned to the capital as director of the Court of Judicial Review, was enfeoffed as Earl of Jincheng, and replaced Cui Yinfu as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 朝隱素有公直之譽，毎御史大夫缺，時議咸許之。

translations.literal: Chaoyin long had a reputation for public integrity; whenever the Censor-in-Chief post was vacant, public opinion always approved him.
translations.idiomatic: Chaoyin had long enjoyed a reputation for public integrity; whenever the post of censor-in-chief fell vacant, public opinion favored him.

sentences.zh: 及居其職，竟無所糾劾，唯煩於細務，時望由是稍減。

translations.literal: When he held the office, in the end there was no impeachment—only preoccupied with trivial matters—public regard accordingly diminished somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office, however, he impeached no one and busied himself with trivial matters; public esteem for him accordingly waned.

sentences.zh: 俄轉太常卿。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，兼判廣州事，仍攝御史大夫，充嶺南采訪處置使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he concurrently judged Guangzhou affairs, still acting as Censor-in-Chief, and served as Investigation and Disposition Commissioner of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: In 733 he concurrently administered Guangzhou affairs, still acting as censor-in-chief, and served as investigation and disposition commissioner for Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 明年，卒於嶺外，年七十，贈吏部尚書，官給靈輿，兼家口給遞還鄕，謚曰貞。

translations.literal: The next year he died beyond the Lingnan frontier, aged seventy; posthumously invested as Minister of the Ministry of Personnel; an official funeral carriage was provided, and his household was given relay transport home; posthumous title Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he died in Lingnan at seventy; posthumously he was made Minister of Personnel; the court provided a funeral carriage and relay transport for his family back to their home district; his posthumous name was Zhen.

sentences.zh: 裴漼裴漼，絳州聞喜人也。

translations.literal: Pei Hui—Pei Hui was a native of Wenxi in Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Hui was a native of Wenxi in Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 世爲著姓。

translations.literal: For generations the clan was a prominent surname.
translations.idiomatic: His was a prominent clan for generations.

sentences.zh: 父琰之，永徽中，爲同州司戸參軍，時年少，美容儀，刺史李崇義初甚輕之。

translations.literal: His father Yanzhi, in the Yonghui era, served as Revenue Section Officer of Tong Prefecture; at the time he was young, with handsome countenance; Governor Li Chongyi initially greatly underestimated him.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yanzhi served in the Yonghui era as revenue section officer of Tong Prefecture. Young and handsome, he was at first greatly underestimated by Governor Li Chongyi.

sentences.zh: 先是，州中有積年舊案數百道，崇義促琰之使斷之，琰之命書吏數人，連紙進筆，斯須剖斷並畢，文翰俱美，且盡與奪之理。

translations.literal: Previously the prefecture had several hundred accumulated old cases of many years; Chongyi urged Yanzhi to decide them; Yanzhi ordered several clerks, continuously supplied paper and advanced pens; in a moment all were decided complete, documents all excellent, and fully covered the logic of granting and denying.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture held several hundred backlogged cases. Chongyi pressed Yanzhi to clear them. Yanzhi set several clerks to work, paper and brushes flowing in succession; in a moment every case was decided, every document polished, and every principle of judgment fully applied.

sentences.zh: 崇義大驚，謝曰：「公何忍藏鋒以成鄙夫之過！」

translations.literal: Chongyi was greatly startled and apologized, saying: "How could you bear to hide your edge and complete this rustic's fault!"
translations.idiomatic: Chongyi was astonished and apologized: "How could you hide your talent and let me make such a fool of myself!"

sentences.zh: 由是大知名，號爲「霹靂手」。

translations.literal: From this he became greatly famous, styled "Thunderbolt Hand."
translations.idiomatic: From that day he was widely known by the nickname "Thunderbolt Hand."

sentences.zh: 後爲永年令，有惠政，人吏刊石頌之。

translations.literal: Later he became magistrate of Yongnian; he had benevolent governance, and officials and people carved stone to praise him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as magistrate of Yongnian, he governed with benevolence, and officials and commoners carved a stone inscription in his praise.

sentences.zh: 歷任倉部郎中，以老疾廢於家。

translations.literal: He served successively as Director in the Ministry of Revenue; due to old age and illness he retired at home.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director in the Ministry of Revenue, then retired home because of old age and illness.

sentences.zh: 漼色養劬勞，十數年不求仕進。

translations.literal: Hui supported his parents with filial devotion through hardship, for more than ten years seeking no official advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Hui devoted himself to supporting his parents and for more than ten years sought no official advancement.

sentences.zh: 父卒後，應大禮舉，拜陳留主簿，累遷監察御史。

translations.literal: After his father's death, he answered the Great Ritual examination, was appointed Chief Clerk of Chenliu, and after successive promotions became Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: After his father's death he passed the Great Ritual examination, was appointed chief clerk of Chenliu, and rose in succession to supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 時吏部侍郎崔湜、鄭愔坐贓爲御史李尚隱所劾，漼同鞫其獄。

translations.literal: At the time Vice Ministers of Personnel Cui Shi and Zheng Yin were impeached for bribery by Censor Li Shangyin; Hui jointly interrogated their cases.
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Ministers Cui Shi and Zheng Yin were impeached for bribery by Censor Li Shangyin, Hui joined in investigating their cases.

sentences.zh: 安樂公主及上官昭容阿黨湜等，漼竟執正奏其罪，甚爲當時所稱。

translations.literal: Princess Anle and Shangguan Zhaorong protected Cui Shi and others as a faction; Hui ultimately upheld justice and memorialized their crimes, greatly praised at the time.
translations.idiomatic: Though Princess Anle and Shangguan Zhaorong shielded Cui Shi and his allies, Hui upheld the law and memorialized their crimes, winning wide praise.

sentences.zh: 三遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he became drafting secretary of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 太極元年，睿宗爲金仙、玉真公主造觀及寺等，時屬春旱，興役不止。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiji, Emperor Ruizong built monasteries and temples for the Princesses Jinxian and Yuzhen; at the time there was spring drought, yet labor conscription did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: In 712 Emperor Ruizong ordered monasteries and temples built for the Princesses Jinxian and Yuzhen. Spring drought afflicted the land, yet conscript labor continued without pause.

sentences.zh: 漼上疏諫曰：

translations.literal: Hui submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Hui submitted a memorial of remonstrance:

sentences.zh: 臣謹案《禮記》春、秋令曰：無聚大眾，無起大役，不可興土功，恐妨農事。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully cites the Book of Rites spring and autumn ordinances: do not gather great multitudes, do not raise great labor, do not undertake earthworks, fearing obstruction of agricultural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant respectfully cites the spring and autumn ordinances of the Book of Rites: do not gather great multitudes, do not launch great projects, do not undertake earthworks—for fear of obstructing the agricultural season.

sentences.zh: 若號令乖度，役使不時，則加疾疫之危，國有水旱之災，此五行之必應也。

translations.literal: If orders violate measure and conscription is untimely, then increases pestilence danger and the state has flood-drought calamity—this is the necessary response of the five phases.
translations.idiomatic: When orders violate proper measure and labor is conscripted out of season, pestilence follows and flood or drought afflicts the realm—such is the inevitable response of the five phases.

sentences.zh: 今自春至夏，時雨愆期，下人憂心，莫知所出。

translations.literal: Now from spring to summer, seasonal rains missed their term; the people below worry, not knowing what to do.
translations.idiomatic: From spring into summer the seasonal rains have failed; the people are anxious and do not know what to do.

sentences.zh: 陛下雖降哀矜之旨，兩都仍有寺觀之作，時旱之應，實此之由。

translations.literal: Though Your Majesty has issued compassionate decrees, both capitals still have temple and monastery construction—the seasonal drought's cause truly lies here.
translations.idiomatic: Though Your Majesty has issued compassionate decrees, construction of temples and monasteries continues in both capitals—and this drought, I fear, is the consequence.

sentences.zh: 且春令告期，東作方始，正是丁壯就功之日，而土木方興，臣恐所妨尤多，所益尤少，耕夫蠶妾，饑寒之源。

translations.literal: Moreover the spring ordinance announces its term, eastern work just beginning—it is precisely when able-bodied men should labor—yet earth and wood construction rises; your servant fears the hindrance is especially great, the benefit especially small; ploughmen and silkworm wives are the source of hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: Spring's ordinance has arrived and farming has just begun—the very season when able-bodied men should be at work—yet construction of earth and timber proceeds. I fear the harm far outweighs the benefit; farmers and silk workers are the source of the people's food and clothing.

sentences.zh: 故《春秋》「莊公三十一年冬，不雨」，《五行傳》以爲「歳三築臺」；

translations.literal: Therefore the Spring and Autumn Annals records "Duke Zhuang, year thirty-one, winter, no rain," and the Treatise on the Five Phases takes it as "three platform constructions in the year";
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Spring and Autumn Annals records that in winter of Duke Zhuang's thirty-first year there was no rain, and the Treatise on the Five Phases attributes it to "three platform constructions in one year";

sentences.zh: 「僖公二十一年夏，大旱」，《五行傳》以「時作南門，勞人興役」。

translations.literal: "Duke Xi, year twenty-one, summer, great drought"—the Treatise on the Five Phases takes it as "then constructing the South Gate, toiling the people with labor."
translations.idiomatic: "In summer of Duke Xi's twenty-first year there was great drought," which the Treatise on the Five Phases attributes to "building the South Gate and exhausting the people with labor."

sentences.zh: 陛下毎以萬方爲念，睿旨殷勤，安國濟人，防微慮遠。

translations.literal: Your Majesty always considers the myriad regions, imperial intent earnest, stabilizing the state and aiding the people, guarding against the subtle and thinking far ahead.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty always has the myriad regions in mind, your intent earnest in stabilizing the state and aiding the people, guarding against small evils and planning far ahead.

sentences.zh: 伏願下明制，發德音，順天時，副人望，兩京公私營造及諸和市木石等並請且停，則蒼生幸甚。

translations.literal: I humbly wish you issue a clear edict, emit a benevolent proclamation, accord with heaven's season, fulfill the people's hopes—all public and private construction in both capitals and all market purchases of timber and stone please halt for now—then the common people would be exceedingly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg Your Majesty to issue a clear edict and a benevolent proclamation, accord with heaven's season, and fulfill the people's hopes: let all public and private construction in both capitals and all market purchases of timber and stone be halted for now—the common people would be deeply grateful.

sentences.zh: 農桑失時，戸口流散，縱寺觀營構，豈救黎元饑寒之弊哉！

translations.literal: Agriculture and sericulture miss their seasons, households scatter and flee—even if temples and monasteries are built, how could they rescue the people from hunger and cold!
translations.idiomatic: When farming and sericulture miss their seasons and households scatter in flight, what good can temple and monastery construction do against hunger and cold!

sentences.zh: 疏奏不報。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted without response.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial received no reply.

sentences.zh: 尋轉兵部侍郎，以銓敘平允，持授一子爲太子通事舍人。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Ministry of War; for fair and equitable selection rating, one of his sons was granted the post of Palace Secretary of the Crown Prince's Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Vice Minister of War; for his fair and equitable personnel ratings, one of his sons was granted the post of secretary in the crown prince's service.

sentences.zh: 開元五年，遷吏部侍郎，典選數年，多所持拔。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaiyuan he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel; he conducted selection for several years and many were promoted by his recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: In 717 he became Vice Minister of Personnel; for several years he ran appointments and promoted many men of talent.

sentences.zh: 再轉黃門侍郎，代韋抗爲御史大夫。

translations.literal: After a second transfer he became Vice Director of the Chancellery and replaced Wei Kang as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was next promoted to vice director of the Chancellery and replaced Wei Kang as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 漼早與張説特相友善，時説在相位，數稱薦之。

translations.literal: Hui early was especially friendly with Zhang Yue; at the time Yue was chancellor and repeatedly praised and recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Hui had long been close to Zhang Yue; when Yue served as chancellor he repeatedly praised and recommended him.

sentences.zh: 漼又善於敷奏，上亦嘉重焉。

translations.literal: Hui was also skilled at memorial presentation; the Emperor also commended and valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was also skilled at presenting memorials, and the emperor valued him highly.

sentences.zh: 由是擢拜吏部尚書，尋轉太子賓客。

translations.literal: Thereby he was promoted to Minister of the Ministry of Personnel and soon transferred to Guest of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly he was promoted to Minister of Personnel and soon made advisor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 漼家世儉約，既久居清要，頗飾妓妾，後庭有綺羅之賞，由是爲時論所譏。

translations.literal: Hui's family for generations was frugal; having long held pure and important offices, he quite adorned himself with courtesans; the rear court had brocade and gauze lavishness—thereby ridiculed in contemporary opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Though his family had been frugal for generations, after long service in high office Hui kept courtesans and lavished brocade and gauze on his household—and was ridiculed for it in public opinion.

sentences.zh: 二十四年卒，年七十餘，贈禮部尚書，謚曰懿。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he died, aged over seventy; posthumously invested as Minister of the Ministry of Rites; posthumous title Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 736 at over seventy; posthumously he was made Minister of Rites and given the posthumous name Yi.

sentences.zh: 漼從祖弟 寬漼從祖弟寬。

translations.literal: Hui's collateral cousin Kuan—Hui's collateral cousin Kuan.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Kuan, Hui's collateral cousin.

sentences.zh: 寬父無晦，袁州刺史。

translations.literal: Kuan's father Wu Hui was Governor of Yuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan's father Wu Hui had been governor of Yuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 寬通略，以文詞進，騎射、彈棋、投壺特妙。

translations.literal: Kuan was broadly capable, advanced through literary skill; horsemanship, archery, bouncing-chess, and pitch-pot were especially excellent.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan was broadly capable and advanced through literary talent; he was especially skilled at horsemanship, archery, bouncing-chess, and pitch-pot.

sentences.zh: 景雲中，爲潤州參軍，刺史韋銑爲按察使，引爲判官，清幹善於剖斷，銑重其才，以女妻之。

translations.literal: In the Jingyun era he served as aide in Run Prefecture; Governor Wei Tiao as investigative commissioner brought him as legal assistant; pure and capable, skilled at judgment; Tiao valued his talent and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingyun era he served as aide in Run Prefecture. When Governor Wei Tiao became investigative commissioner, he took Kuan as his legal assistant. Kuan was upright, capable, and skilled at judgment; Tiao valued his talent and gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 後應拔萃，舉河南丞。

translations.literal: Later he passed the exceptional selection and was promoted to Assistant Governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he passed the exceptional selection examination and was promoted to assistant governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 再轉爲長安尉。

translations.literal: After a second transfer he became Sheriff of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: After another transfer he became sheriff of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 時宇文融爲侍御史，括天下田戸，使奏差爲江南東道勾當租庸地稅兼覆田判官。

translations.literal: At the time Yuwen Rong was Attendant Censor, registering land and households throughout the realm; he had him memorialized and dispatched as Commissioner for rent, corvée, and land tax in Jiangnan East Circuit, concurrently agricultural inspector and legal assistant.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yuwen Rong, serving as attendant censor, was registering land and households throughout the realm; he had Kuan memorialized and dispatched as commissioner for rent, corvée, and land tax in Jiangnan East Circuit, concurrently serving as agricultural inspector and legal assistant.

sentences.zh: 轉太常博士。

translations.literal: Transferred to be Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 禮部擬國忌之辰享廟用樂，下太常，寬深達禮節，特建新意，以爲廟尊忌卑則登歌，廟卑忌尊則去龠。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Rites proposed using music when offering at the ancestral temple on the national mourning day and sent the matter down to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. Kuan was deeply versed in ritual propriety and specially devised a new principle: when the temple rank was higher and the mourning rank lower, perform the ascent hymn; when the temple rank was lower and the mourning rank higher, remove the flutes.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ministry of Rites proposed using music for temple offerings on a national mourning day and referred the question to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Kuan, deeply versed in ritual, devised a new rule: if the temple's rank outranked the mourning observance, the ascent hymn should be sung; if the mourning observance outranked the temple, the flutes should be omitted.

sentences.zh: 中書令張説謂寬明識，舉而行之。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Zhang Yue said Kuan was clear-sighted and had the proposal adopted and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Zhang Yue declared that Kuan was far-sighted and had his proposal adopted and put into practice.

sentences.zh: 再遷爲刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: After another transfer he became Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: After another promotion he became vice director of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 有萬騎將軍馬崇正晝殺人，時開府、霍國公王毛仲恩幸用事，將鬻其獄，寬執之不回。

translations.literal: The Wanqi General Ma Chongzheng murdered someone in broad daylight. At the time the Director of Kai Prefecture, Duke Huo of the Kingdom Wang Maozhong, favored by imperial grace and wielding power, was about to sell the case; Kuan held firm and did not yield.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wanqi General Ma Chongzheng murdered a man in broad daylight, Wang Maozhong, Duke of Huo and director of Kai Prefecture, then a favorite at court wielding great power, was about to corrupt the trial—but Kuan held firm and would not bend.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書蕭嵩爲河西節度使，奏寬及郭虛己爲判官，累年專見委任，嵩加中書令，寬歷中書舍人、御史中丞、兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Minister of War Xiao Song served as military commissioner of Hexi and memorialized Kuan and Guo Xuji as legal assistants. For many years he was specially entrusted; when Song was promoted to Chief Minister, Kuan successively held posts as Secretariat drafter, Censor-in-Chief, and Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister of War Xiao Song became military commissioner of Hexi, he recommended Kuan and Guo Xuji as his legal assistants and entrusted them exclusively for many years. After Song was made chief minister, Kuan rose through the posts of secretariat drafter, censor-in-chief, and vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 開元二十一年冬，裴耀卿以黃門侍郎知政事，扈從出關，知江、淮轉運，於河陰置倉，奏寬爲戸部侍郎，爲其副。

translations.literal: In the winter of the twenty-first year of Kaiyuan, Pei Yaocheng as Vice Director of the Palace Domestic Service handled state affairs, accompanied the emperor out of the pass to oversee Jiang-Huai transport, set up granaries at Heyin, and memorialized Kuan as Vice Minister of Revenue as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of 733, Pei Yaocheng, serving as vice director of the Palace Domestic Service and handling state affairs, accompanied the emperor beyond the pass to oversee transport on the Yangtze and Huai rivers. When he established granaries at Heyin, he recommended Kuan as vice minister of revenue to serve as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 寬性友愛，弟兄多宦達，子侄亦有名稱，於東京立第同居，八院相對，甥侄皆有休憩所，擊鼓而食，當世榮之。

translations.literal: Kuan was by nature fraternal; many of his brothers achieved official success, and his sons and nephews also had renown. In the Eastern Capital they built a residence and lived together—eight courtyards facing one another; nephews and nieces all had resting quarters; they beat a drum to summon meals—the age regarded it with honor.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan was devoted to his family. Many of his brothers rose to high office, and his sons and nephews were also well known. In the Eastern Capital they built a shared residence of eight facing courtyards, with quarters for every nephew and niece, and summoned the household to meals by beating a drum—a way of life the age admired.

sentences.zh: 選吏部侍郎，及玄宗還京，又改蒲州刺史。

translations.literal: Selected as Vice Minister of Personnel; when Xuanzong returned to the capital, he was again changed to Governor of Pu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected as vice minister of personnel, and when Xuanzong returned to the capital, he was reassigned as governor of Pu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 州境久旱，入境，雨乃大浹。

translations.literal: The prefecture had long suffered drought; when he entered his jurisdiction, rain fell in great abundance.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture had long been in drought, but when he entered his jurisdiction, rain fell in torrents.

sentences.zh: 遷河南尹，不附權貴，務於恤隱，政乃大理。

translations.literal: Transferred to Intendant of Henan; he did not attach himself to the powerful and noble, devoted himself to relieving distress, and governance became greatly orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to intendant of Henan, he refused to court the powerful, devoted himself to relieving the people's hardships, and brought the administration to good order.

sentences.zh: 改左金吾衞大將軍，一年，除太原尹，賜紫金魚袋。

translations.literal: Changed to General-in-Chief of the Left Gold Crow Guard; after one year, appointed Intendant of Taiyuan, granted the gold and purple fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general-in-chief of the Left Gold Crow Guard, and after one year was appointed intendant of Taiyuan and granted the gold-and-purple fish tally.

sentences.zh: 玄宗賦詩而餞之，曰：「德比岱雲布，心如晉水清。」

translations.literal: Xuanzong composed a poem to fare him well, saying: "Your virtue spreads like clouds over Mount Tai; your heart is clear as the waters of Jinyang."
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong composed a poem to send him off, saying: "Your virtue spreads like clouds over Mount Tai; your heart is clear as the waters of Jinyang."

sentences.zh: 天寶初，除陳留太守，兼采訪使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, appointed Governor of Chenliu, concurrently investigative commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianbao era he was appointed governor of Chenliu and concurrently made investigative commissioner.

sentences.zh: 尋而范陽節度李適之入爲御史大夫，除寬范陽節度兼采訪使河北替之。

translations.literal: Soon Li Shizhi, military commissioner of Fanyang, entered the capital as Censor-in-Chief; Kuan was appointed military commissioner of Fanyang and investigative commissioner of Hebei to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Li Shizhi, military commissioner of Fanyang, entered the capital as censor-in-chief, and Kuan was appointed military commissioner of Fanyang and investigative commissioner of Hebei to replace him.

sentences.zh: 其年，又加御史大夫，時北平軍使烏承恩恃以蕃酋與中貴通，恣求貨賄，寬以法按之。

translations.literal: That year he was additionally made Censor-in-Chief. At the time Beiping Army envoy Wu Chengen, relying on his status as a frontier chieftain and connections with palace eunuchs, wantonly sought bribes; Kuan investigated him according to law.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he was also made censor-in-chief. Wu Chengen, envoy of the Beiping Army, relied on his standing as a frontier chieftain and his ties to palace eunuchs to extort bribes at will; Kuan investigated him by the book.

sentences.zh: 檀州刺史何僧獻生口數十人，寬悉命歸之，故夷夏感悅。

translations.literal: Tan Prefecture Governor He Xianxian had captives numbering several tens of persons; Kuan ordered them all returned home, so barbarians and Chinese alike were moved with gratification.
translations.idiomatic: When Tan Prefecture governor He Xianxian held several dozen captives, Kuan ordered them all sent home, to the delight of both frontier peoples and Han subjects.

sentences.zh: 三載，以安祿山爲范陽節度，寬爲戸部尚書、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the third year, An Lushan was made military commissioner of Fanyang, and Kuan was made Minister of Revenue and concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianbao, An Lushan was made military commissioner of Fanyang, and Kuan was appointed minister of revenue and concurrent censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 玄宗素重寬，日加恩顧。

translations.literal: Xuanzong had long valued Kuan and daily increased his favor and attention.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong had long held Kuan in high regard and daily showered him with favor.

sentences.zh: 刑部尚書裴敦復討海賊回，頗張賊勢，又廣敘功以開請托之路，寬嘗幾微奏之。

translations.literal: Minister of Justice Pei Dunfu returned from campaigning against sea pirates; he greatly exaggerated the enemy's strength and also broadly narrated merit to open a path for solicitation; Kuan once subtly memorialized about this.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister of Justice Pei Dunfu returned from campaigning against sea pirates, he greatly inflated the enemy's strength and padded his account of merit to open the door to favor-seeking; Kuan once submitted a subtle memorial on the matter.

sentences.zh: 居數日，有河北將士入奏，盛言寬在范陽能政，塞上思之，玄宗嗟賞久之。

translations.literal: Within several days, officers and soldiers from Hebei entered a memorial, lavishly praising Kuan's capable governance at Fanyang and how the frontier missed him; Xuanzong sighed and admired this for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few days, officers and soldiers from Hebei memorialized the throne, praising Kuan's able governance at Fanyang and saying how the frontier missed him; Xuanzong sighed in admiration for a long while.

sentences.zh: 李林甫懼其入相，又惡寬與李適之善，乃呼裴敦復，且以寬之語告之。

translations.literal: Li Linfu feared Kuan would enter the chancellorship, and also hated that Kuan was friendly with Li Shizhi; he summoned Pei Dunfu and told him what Kuan had said.
translations.idiomatic: Li Linfu feared that Kuan might enter the chancellorship and also resented his friendship with Li Shizhi, so he summoned Pei Dunfu and told him what Kuan had said.

sentences.zh: 敦復使氣性疏，與寬素不相下，以爲林甫推誠於己，因願結之，且訴其冤。

translations.literal: Dunfu was hot-tempered and careless by nature; he and Kuan had never been deferential to each other. Thinking Linfu was showing sincerity toward him, he therefore wished to ally with him and also complained of his injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Dunfu was hot-tempered and careless by nature, and he and Kuan had never gotten along. Believing that Linfu was showing him genuine goodwill, he sought an alliance with him and complained of the wrong done to him.

sentences.zh: 先是，寬以親故名囑敦復，求請軍功。

translations.literal: Previously, Kuan, relying on a close relation's name, had asked Dunfu to request military merit.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Kuan had asked Dunfu to secure military merit for a close relative.

sentences.zh: 至是敦復氣憤發其事，林甫曰：「公宜速奏，無後於人。」

translations.literal: At this Dunfu in anger exposed the affair. Linfu said: "You ought to memorialize quickly—do not let others get ahead of you."
translations.idiomatic: Now Dunfu, in a fit of anger, exposed the affair. Linfu said, "You should memorialize at once—do not let anyone beat you to it."

sentences.zh: 尋而敦復扈從幸溫泉宮，寬在京城未發。

translations.literal: Soon Dunfu accompanied the emperor to the Hot Spring Palace; Kuan had not yet departed from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Dunfu accompanied the emperor to the Hot Spring Palace, while Kuan had not yet left the capital.

sentences.zh: 遇有敦復下軍將程藏曜、郎將曹鑒。

translations.literal: He encountered Dunfu's subordinate army commander Cheng Zangyao and commander Cao Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He came upon Dunfu's subordinate army commander Cheng Zangyao and commander Cao Jian.

sentences.zh: 鑒，郴州富人；

translations.literal: Jian was a wealthy man of Chen Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Jian was a wealthy man of Chen Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 藏曜，嶺南首領之子。

translations.literal: Zangyao was the son of a Lingnan chieftain.
translations.idiomatic: Zangyao was the son of a Lingnan chieftain.

sentences.zh: 皆有他事，與人詣臺告訴，寬受其狀，捕鑒等鞫之。

translations.literal: Both had other matters; people came to the censorate to lodge complaints. Kuan accepted their petitions and arrested Jian and others for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: Both were implicated in other offenses, and people came to the censorate to lodge complaints. Kuan accepted their petitions and had Jian and the others arrested for interrogation.

sentences.zh: 敦復判官太常博士王悅聞之，謂寬求其過，連夜詣湯所以告。

translations.literal: Dunfu's legal assistant, Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Wang Yue, heard of it, saying Kuan was seeking his fault; he went overnight to where Dunfu was to report it.
translations.idiomatic: When Dunfu's legal assistant Wang Yue, an erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, heard of it, he concluded that Kuan was hunting for a pretext against his master and went overnight to Dunfu's quarters to report it.

sentences.zh: 敦復大懼，促裝待罪，因令子婿以五百金賂於貴妃姊楊三娘。

translations.literal: Dunfu was greatly afraid, hurriedly packed to await punishment, and had his son-in-law bribe Yang San Niang, elder sister of the Noble Consort, with five hundred gold.
translations.idiomatic: Dunfu was terrified, hurriedly packed to await punishment, and had his son-in-law pay five hundred gold in bribes to Yang San Niang, elder sister of the Noble Consort.

sentences.zh: 楊氏遽爲言之，明日貶寬爲睢陽太守。

translations.literal: The Yang clan hastily spoke for him; the next day Kuan was demoted to Governor of Suiyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Yang clan quickly interceded on his behalf, and the next day Kuan was demoted to governor of Suiyang.

sentences.zh: 寬以清簡爲政，故所蒞人皆愛之。

translations.literal: Kuan governed with purity and simplicity, so people everywhere he served loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan governed with purity and restraint, and the people everywhere he served loved him for it.

sentences.zh: 當時望爲宰輔。

translations.literal: At the time he was expected to become chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: At the time he was widely expected to reach the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 及韋堅構禍，寬又以親累貶爲安陸別駕員外置。

translations.literal: When Wei Jian brought disaster upon himself, Kuan was again demoted through guilt by kinship to supernumerary Vice Governor of Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Jian brought ruin upon himself, Kuan was again demoted by association to a supernumerary post as vice governor of Anlu.

sentences.zh: 林甫使羅希奭南殺李適之，紆路至安陸過，擬怖死之。

translations.literal: Linfu sent Luo Xiyi south to kill Li Shizhi; taking a circuitous route through Anlu, he planned to frighten Kuan to death.
translations.idiomatic: Linfu sent Luo Xiyi south to kill Li Shizhi; taking a roundabout route through Anlu, he planned to terrify Kuan to death.

sentences.zh: 寬叩頭祈請，希奭不宿而過。

translations.literal: Kuan kowtowed and pleaded; Xiyi did not stay the night but passed on.
translations.idiomatic: Kuan kowtowed and begged for mercy; Xiyi did not even spend the night but passed on.

sentences.zh: 寬又懼死，上表請爲僧，詔不許。

translations.literal: Kuan again feared death and memorialized requesting to become a monk; an edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Still fearing for his life, Kuan memorialized asking to become a monk, but an edict refused his request.

sentences.zh: 然崇信釋典，常與僧徒往來，焚香禮懺，老而彌篤。

translations.literal: Yet he revered the Buddhist canon, often associated with monks, burned incense and performed repentance rituals—growing more earnest in old age.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, he revered the Buddhist scriptures, kept company with monks, burned incense and performed repentance rites, and grew only more devout with age.

sentences.zh: 累遷東海太守、襄州采訪使、銀青光祿大夫，轉馮翊太守，入拜禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions: Governor of Donghai, investigative commissioner of Xiang Prefecture, Grand Master with Silver-Green Tally; transferred to Governor of Fengyi; entered court as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Through successive promotions he became governor of Donghai, investigative commissioner of Xiang Prefecture, and grand master with silver-green tally; then governor of Fengyi; and finally entered court as minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 十四載卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he died, aged seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 755, at the age of seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 詔贈太子少傅，賻帛一百五十段、粟一百五十石。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously invested him as Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince, with condolence gifts of one hundred fifty bolts of silk and one hundred fifty shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made him junior tutor of the crown prince and granted condolence gifts of one hundred fifty bolts of silk and one hundred fifty shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 兄弟八人，皆明經及第，入臺省、典郡者五人。

translations.literal: Eight brothers, all passed the Mingjing examination and entered office; five served in the censorate and secretariat or governed prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Of eight brothers, all passed the Classics examination; five served in the censorate and secretariat or governed prefectures.

sentences.zh: 寬歿之後，弟珣爲河內郡太守。

translations.literal: After Kuan's death, his younger brother Xun became Governor of Henei Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Kuan's death, his younger brother Xun became governor of Henei Commandery.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，以執父喪，將投闕庭，恐累其母，乃詣河東節度訴誠而退。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, because he was observing mourning for his father and about to go submit himself at the palace gates, fearing to implicate his mother, he went to the Hedong commissioner to declare his loyalty and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, Xun was in mourning for his father and about to surrender himself at the palace gates, but fearing to implicate his mother, he went instead to the Hedong military commissioner to declare his loyalty and then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 後在母憂，又陷史思明，授其偽官委任，使弟朗密奉表疏至上京。

translations.literal: Later, during mourning for his mother, he again fell into Shi Siming's hands; granted a false office and entrusted with duties, he had his younger brother Lang secretly deliver memorials to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while mourning his mother, he again fell into Shi Siming's hands; though given a post in the rebel administration, he entrusted his younger brother Lang with secretly delivering memorials to the capital.

sentences.zh: 代宗時，爲左司郎中、兼侍御史、河東道租庸判官。

translations.literal: During Daizong's reign, he was Director of the Left Bureau of the Ministry of Personnel, concurrent Attendant Censor, and rent and corvée legal assistant for Hedong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Daizong he served as director of the left bureau of the Ministry of Personnel, concurrent attendant censor, and legal assistant for rent and corvée in Hedong Circuit.

sentences.zh: 王丘王丘，光祿卿同皎從兄子也。

translations.literal: Wang Qiu—Wang Qiu was the son of the paternal cousin of Tong Jiao, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiu was the son of the paternal cousin of Tong Jiao, who had served as director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 父同晊，左庶子。

translations.literal: His father Tong Zhi was Left Supervisor of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tong Zhi had been left supervisor of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 丘年十一，童子舉擢第，時類皆以誦經爲課，丘獨以屬文見擢，由是知名。

translations.literal: At age eleven Qiu passed the Youth Examination; contemporaries all took reciting classics as the test—Qiu alone was selected for literary composition, and from this became known.
translations.idiomatic: At eleven Qiu passed the youth examination; while others were tested on reciting the classics, he alone was chosen for his literary composition, and from that he became known.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，又應制舉，拜奉禮郎。

translations.literal: At age twenty he also passed the imperial special examination and was appointed Gentleman for Ritual Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: In his early twenties he also passed the special imperial examination and was appointed gentleman for ritual attendance.

sentences.zh: 丘神氣清古，而誌行修潔，尤善詞賦，族人左庶子方慶及御史大夫魏元忠皆稱薦之。

translations.literal: Qiu's bearing was pure and antique; his will and conduct refined and clean; he was especially skilled at rhapsody and fu. His clansman Left Supervisor Fang Qing and Censor-in-Chief Wei Yuanzhong all praised and recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu had a pure, antique bearing and conduct of refined integrity; he was especially skilled at rhapsody and fu. His clansman Fang Qing, left supervisor of the Palace Library, and Censor-in-Chief Wei Yuanzhong both praised and recommended him.

sentences.zh: 長安中，自偃師主簿擢第，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: During the Chang'an era, from Record Keeper of Yanshi he passed selection and was appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an era he passed selection from his post as record keeper of Yanshi and was appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 開元初，累遷考功員外郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan, through successive promotions he became Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel in charge of examinations.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Kaiyuan era he rose through successive promotions to vice director of the Ministry of Personnel in charge of examinations.

sentences.zh: 先是，考功舉人，請托大行，取士頗濫，毎年至數百人，丘一切核其實材，登科者僅滿百人。

translations.literal: Previously, in examining candidates for the Ministry of Personnel, solicitation was rampant and selection was quite lax—each year reaching several hundred persons. Qiu in every case verified their actual talent; those who passed numbered barely a full hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, the examination office was rife with favor-seeking and lax in selecting candidates, passing several hundred each year. Qiu verified every candidate's real ability, and those who passed numbered barely a hundred.

sentences.zh: 議者以爲自則天已後凡數十年，無如丘者，其後席豫、嚴挺之爲其次焉。

translations.literal: Commentators held that since Empress Wu's time, for several decades there had been none like Qiu; after him Xi Yu and Yan Tingzhi were next.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators held that in the several decades since Empress Wu's time there had been no examiner like Qiu; Xi Yu and Yan Tingzhi ranked next after him.

sentences.zh: 三遷紫微舍人，以知制誥之勤，加朝散大夫，再轉吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became Secretariat drafter of Ziwei; for diligence in drafting edicts he was given Grand Master for Dispersed Merit and after two transfers became Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he became a Ziwei secretariat drafter; for diligence in drafting edicts he was given the rank of grand master for dispersed merit, and after two further transfers became vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 典選累年，甚稱平允。

translations.literal: He managed selections for many years and was greatly praised as fair and equitable.
translations.idiomatic: He managed personnel selections for many years and was widely praised for fairness.

sentences.zh: 擢用山陰尉孫逖、桃林尉張鏡微、湖城尉張晉明、進士王泠然，皆稱一時之秀。

translations.literal: He promoted Shan Yin Sheriff Sun Ti, Taolin Sheriff Zhang Jingwei, Hucheng Sheriff Zhang Jinming, and jinshi Wang Lengan—all acclaimed as outstanding talents of the age.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted Sun Ti, sheriff of Shanyin; Zhang Jingwei, sheriff of Taolin; Zhang Jinming, sheriff of Hucheng; and the jinshi Wang Lengan—all hailed as outstanding talents of their day.

sentences.zh: 俄換尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Soon exchanged to Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was transferred to left vice minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十一年，拜黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, appointed Vice Director of the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was appointed vice director of the Palace Domestic Service.

sentences.zh: 其年，山東旱儉，朝議選朝臣爲刺史以撫貧民，制曰：「昔咎繇與禹言曰：『在知人，在安人。』

translations.literal: That year Shandong suffered drought and famine; court deliberation chose court officials as governors to comfort the impoverished people. An edict said: "In ancient times Gao Yao said to Yu: 'Know men; settle men.
translations.idiomatic: That year Shandong suffered drought and famine, and the court chose senior officials to serve as governors to relieve the poor. An edict declared: "In antiquity Gao Yao said to Yu, 'The task lies in knowing men and in settling men.

sentences.zh: 此皆念存邦本，光於帝載，乾乾夕惕，無忘一日。

translations.literal: All these thoughts preserve the foundation of the state, illumine the imperial record—diligent morning and evening, never forgetting for a day.
translations.idiomatic: These words show concern for the foundation of the state and light the imperial record—diligent morning and evening, never forgetting even for a day.

sentences.zh: 而長吏或不稱，蒼生或未寧，深思循良，以矯過弊，仍重諸侯之選，故自朝廷始之。」

translations.literal: Yet local chiefs are sometimes unfit, and the common people are sometimes unrested; deeply reflecting on the upright and good to correct excess and abuse, we again weight the selection of regional lords—therefore beginning from the court itself."
translations.idiomatic: Yet local officials are sometimes unfit, and the people are sometimes left unsettled. Deeply mindful of upright governance to correct past abuses, we again weigh the choice of regional governors, and therefore begin with appointments from the court itself."

sentences.zh: 於是以丘爲懷州刺史，又以中書侍郎崔沔等數人皆爲山東諸州刺史。

translations.literal: Accordingly Qiu was made Governor of Huai Prefecture, and several others including Vice Chief Minister Cui Hao were all made governors of Shandong prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly Qiu was made governor of Huai Prefecture, and several others, including Vice Chief Minister Cui Hao, were all appointed governors of Shandong prefectures.

sentences.zh: 至任，皆無可稱，唯丘在職清嚴，人吏甚畏慕之。

translations.literal: Upon assuming office, none could be praised; only Qiu in office was pure and strict, and officials and commoners greatly feared and admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office, none of them distinguished themselves; only Qiu governed with purity and strictness, and officials and commoners alike feared and admired him.

sentences.zh: 俄又分知吏部選事，入爲尚書左丞，丁父憂去職，服闋，拜右散騎常侍，仍知制誥。

translations.literal: Soon he again shared in managing personnel selections; entered as Left Vice Minister; left office on father's mourning; after mourning period, appointed Right Regular Attendant of the Imperial Secretariat, still drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he again shared in managing personnel selections, entered court as left vice minister, left office to mourn his father, and after the mourning period was appointed right regular attendant of the Imperial Secretariat, still drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，侍中裴光庭病卒，中書令蕭嵩與丘有舊，將薦丘知政事，丘知而固辭，且盛推尚書右丞韓休，嵩因而奏之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, Chief Minister Pei Guangting died of illness; Chief Minister Xiao Song was old friends with Qiu and was about to recommend Qiu to handle state affairs; Qiu learned of it and firmly declined, and greatly recommended Right Vice Minister Han Xiu; Song therefore memorialized him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year Chief Minister Pei Guangting died of illness. Chief Minister Xiao Song, an old friend of Qiu's, was about to recommend Qiu for the chancellorship, but Qiu learned of it and firmly declined, warmly recommending Right Vice Minister Han Xiu instead; Song memorialized Xiu accordingly.

sentences.zh: 及休作相，遂薦丘代崔琳爲御史大夫。

translations.literal: When Xiu became chancellor, he then recommended Qiu to replace Cui Lin as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Xiu became chancellor, he recommended Qiu to replace Cui Lin as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 丘既訥於言詞，敷奏多不稱旨。

translations.literal: Qiu was slow of speech; his memorial presentations often did not meet the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu was slow of speech, and his memorial presentations often failed to please the emperor.

sentences.zh: 俄轉太子賓客，襲父爵宿預男，尋以疾拜禮部尚書，仍聽致仕。

translations.literal: Soon transferred to Guest of the Crown Prince; inherited his father's title Baron of Suyu; soon due to illness appointed Minister of Rites, and permitted to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made advisor to the crown prince, inherited his father's title Baron of Suyu, and shortly afterward, owing to illness, was appointed minister of rites and permitted to retire.

sentences.zh: 丘雖歷要職，固守清儉，未嘗受人饋遺，第宅輿馬，稱爲敝陋。

translations.literal: Though Qiu held important posts, he steadfastly maintained purity and frugality; never accepted gifts; his residence and carriage were called shabby.
translations.idiomatic: Though Qiu had held important posts, he steadfastly maintained purity and frugality, never accepted gifts, and his house and carriage were said to be shabby.

sentences.zh: 致仕之後，藥餌殆將不給。

translations.literal: After retirement, medicine and food were scarcely sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: After retirement he could scarcely afford medicine and food.

sentences.zh: 上聞而嘉嘆，下制曰：「王丘夙負良材，累升茂秩，比縁疾疹，假以優閑。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard and commended this with sighs, issuing an edict: "Wang Qiu from of old bore fine talent, through successive promotions rose to flourishing rank; recently owing to illness, granted leisure and ease.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this he sighed in admiration and issued an edict: "Wang Qiu has long possessed fine talent and rose through flourishing ranks; recently, owing to illness, he was granted a life of ease.

sentences.zh: 聞其家道屢空，醫藥靡給，久此從宦，遂無余資。

translations.literal: I hear his household way is repeatedly empty, medicine scarcely provided; long in office, thus without surplus resources.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that his household is repeatedly destitute and that he lacks even for medicine; after long service in office he has no savings left.

sentences.zh: 持操若斯，古人何遠！

translations.literal: Maintaining conduct like this—how far from the ancients!
translations.idiomatic: To maintain such integrity—how little he falls short of the ancients!

sentences.zh: 且優賢之義，方冊所先，周急之宜，沮勸攸在。

translations.literal: Moreover, the principle of honoring the worthy is what written records put first; the propriety of relieving urgency is where encouragement and restraint lie.
translations.idiomatic: The duty to honor the worthy comes first in the written records, and relieving distress is how encouragement and restraint are made real.

sentences.zh: 其俸祿一事已上，並宜全給，式表殊常之澤，用旌貞白之吏。」

translations.literal: His salary from one item upward should all be fully granted, thereby displaying extraordinary favor and commending an upright and pure official."
translations.idiomatic: His salary in full, from the lowest item upward, shall continue to be paid, to show extraordinary favor and commend an official of pure integrity."

sentences.zh: 天寶二年卒，贈荊州大都督。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianbao he died; posthumously invested as Grand Protector of Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 743 and was posthumously made grand protector of Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰史臣曰：有唐之興，綿歷年所，骨鯁清廉之士，懷忠抱義之臣，臺省之間，駕肩接武。

translations.literal: The historian says: The historian says: From the rise of Tang through many years, upright and incorruptible men, ministers cherishing loyalty and embracing righteousness—in the censorate and secretariat they walked shoulder to shoulder.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: From the founding of Tang through many years, upright and incorruptible men and ministers who cherished loyalty and embraced righteousness filled the censorate and secretariat, walking shoulder to shoulder.

sentences.zh: 但時有夷險，道有汙隆，用與不用而已。

translations.literal: Yet times had peace and peril; the Way had decline and ascent—used or not used, that was all.
translations.idiomatic: Yet times had their ease and peril, and the Way its rise and fall—whether men were employed or passed over was all.

sentences.zh: 睿、玄之世，若李傑、畢構、蘇珦、鄭惟忠、王志愔、盧從願、裴漼、王丘並位歷亞臺，名德兼著。

translations.literal: In the eras of Ruizong and Xuanzong, men such as Li Jie, Bi Gou, Su Xian, Zheng Weizhong, Wang Zhiyin, Lu Congyuan, Pei Hui, and Wang Qiu all held posts of the secondary censorate, combining fame and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In the reigns of Ruizong and Xuanzong, men such as Li Jie, Bi Gou, Su Xian, Zheng Weizhong, Wang Zhiyin, Lu Congyuan, Pei Hui, and Wang Qiu all held secondary censorate posts and combined fame with virtue.

sentences.zh: 如尹思貞、李朝隱折李承嘉、竇懷貞，辱閭興貴、趙常奴，詩人所謂不畏強禦者也。

translations.literal: Such as Yin Sizhen and Li Chaoyin, who broke Li Chengjia and Dou Huaizhen, humiliated Lu Xinggui and Zhao Changnu—what the poets call those who do not fear the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Yin Sizhen and Li Chaoyin, who broke Li Chengjia and Dou Huaizhen and humiliated Lu Xinggui and Zhao Changnu, were what the poets meant by those who do not fear the powerful.

sentences.zh: 解琬總兵朔野，料敵如神，功遂身退，深知止足，茲亦有足多也。

translations.literal: Jie Wan commanded troops in the northern frontier, anticipated the enemy like a god; merit achieved, body withdrawn, deeply knowing where to stop—this too is abundantly praiseworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Jie Wan commanded armies on the northern frontier and anticipated the enemy like a god; when his work was done he withdrew, deeply knowing where to stop—this too is abundantly worthy of praise.

sentences.zh: 贊贊曰：尚書亞臺，京尹方伯。

translations.literal: In praise: In praise: Vice ministers of the secretariat, intendant of the capital, regional governors.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: Vice ministers of the secretariat, intendant of the capital, regional governors.

sentences.zh: 我朝重官，云誰稱職？

translations.literal: Our court's weighty offices—who fulfilled their duties?
translations.idiomatic: In our dynasty's weightiest offices, who truly fulfilled their duties?

sentences.zh: 傑、構、珦、忠，能竭其力。

translations.literal: Jie, Gou, Xian, Zhong—each exhausted his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Jie, Gou, Xian, and Zhong each exhausted their strength.

sentences.zh: 愔、願、漼、丘，聿修厥德。

translations.literal: Yin, Yuan, Hui, Qiu—each cultivated his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Yin, Yuan, Hui, and Qiu each cultivated their virtue.

sentences.zh: 貞蔑大僚，隱繩貴戚。

translations.literal: Zhen scorned great officials; Yin bound the noble kin.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhen scorned great officials; Chaoyin restrained the noble kin.

sentences.zh: 琬馳令名，燕、蜀之北。

translations.literal: Wan spread a fine reputation north of Yan and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Wan spread a fine reputation across the lands north of Yan and Shu.
